#1993. Now entering the debate on whether Bruno Guimaraes is returning Toon hero or Toon turncoat

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

I have been reading lately, with interest, the conversations surrounding the return of Bruno Guimaraes to St James’ Park this coming weekend (Saturday 21st November)

Opinion seems to be split as to what kind of reception our former captain should receive if he is selected to face us on Saturday evening.

Since leaving Newcastle United, Bruno Guimaraes hasn’t been an automatic starter, so we may not have the chance to show him our collective feelings either way.

From what I am reading the camp seems to be split directly down the middle between “Bruno Guimaraes is a hero who led us to our first silverware in decades”, to “Bruno Guimaraes is a traitor who went all out to manufacture a move away from the club.”

Looking back now at the summer dealings it’s easier to reflect on what happened and why the players who left, did.

In my opinion , it was only a matter of time before Sandro left us, his heart never seemed in the Northeast, neither does it in North London to be honest, the only time I think we will see him truly happy is when he is plying his trade back in Italy, unfortunately for him it doesn’t look as if Italian football could subsidise that kind of financial arrangement.

Again, in my opinion the same can be said about Anthony Gordon, I liked the lad but also got the impression he thought he was destined for a bigger club, something which was proven to be true.

I just got the impression he thought he was too big a name for the club and it was a matter of time before he left. The fact he went abroad seemed to make the move slightly more palatable as a Newcastle fan.

And on to Bruno, I love(d) the bloke, I was stood in the away section of the Stadium of light, with 7,000 others, 3-0 up and watched him slide tackle on our own goal line and celebrate as if he had scored.

I loved his passion and enthusiasm for the game and the Toon. He could drive and win a game single handedly by grabbing the team by the scruff of the neck and pushing the team forward.

I loved his speech at the presentation in Leases Park and the way he appreciated the character of the Northeast.

Will I boo him if he plays on Saturday? 100%. This is not out of spite; I take this decision more so on a few factors.

Bruno Guimaraes is a confidence player; we have seen this ourselves over the years. We know he feels bad about leaving, he has made a few statements leading up to the game about the toughest decision he has had to make-blah blah blah etc.

But, he went out of his way to hire a super-agent in Kia Joorabchian to help get a move away. Not the actions of a player in love with the glorious Northeast.

He had opportunities to soften the blow leaving, many times over the course of the 2026 World Cup, but chose the cowards way out with total silence, despite the obvious affect it would have on the fans

Let’s get at him, rattle him, affect his confidence, and take the roof off every time Dan Burn cuts him in half, maybe that will be enough to unsettle him and his teammates.

Newcastle United are in a transitional period as a team, but I still feel on a Saturday evening kick off, with a crowd fuelled with day drinking we can beat anyone..

Maybe spare applause for Bruno Guimaraes at the end for his service to the club, I will.

#1992. West Ham Winger Faces Another Fitness Test As Parker Waits

West Ham United are facing something of a dilemma over Manor Solomon, with Israel reportedly considering bringing the winger back into the team for Tuesday’s Nations League clash against Austria. The 26-year-old has been struggling with back pain during the international break, although Israel manager Ran Ben-Shimon has suggested that he is feeling better after returning to training.

According to Sport5, Solomon could now be in contention for the Austria fixture. That follows comments from Ben-Shimon suggesting the player had trained and was feeling better, although his fitness would need to be reassessed.

For West Ham manager Scott Parker, however, the situation presents an interesting dilemma. We desperately need the old Manor Solomon back, but I wonder whether another international appearance is really what the player needs right now.

Manor Solomon representing Israel during a difficult international break. The West Ham winger has been carrying a back injury since October

Look, I’m caught between a rock and a hard place on this one.

There is part of me that hopes Solomon gets a game, so he can get back to form. Because there’s no doubt about it, West Ham have a far bigger chance of getting promoted this season if Manor Solomon is back to the sort of form he was in when he played for Leeds in the Championship.

Clearly Scott Parker has faith in him because he has seen how destructive he can be in that division. Getting that player back would be a significant boost for the Hammers, particularly with the Championship promotion race starting to get serious.

But, and it’s a big but, we have had complaints of back injury during the October internationals, and we’ve already had it during this international break.

As I reported earlier in October, a West Ham source confirmed that Solomon was in considerable pain after an exhausting international schedule. More recently, we reported on his latest back problem, which restricted his training with Israel.

There is also part of me that wonders whether we would not have been better served, and the player himself, actually resting up, getting some medical treatment, or even being given ten days off completely to recuperate and joining back up with the squad for the last few days of training before the Preston game.

As things stand, there’s nothing in his recent form that suggests he could start and should start against Preston. And without him being on the training pitch during this international break to impress Scott Parker, he’s not going to be able to catch the manager’s eye.

Edvin Austbø has certainly given Parker something to think about on the left wing. Indeed, Austbø’s recent performances have highlighted the competition for Solomon’s place, and I suspect the Norwegian is currently ahead of him in the pecking order.

But I don’t want to write off Solomon. We know what he’s capable of producing in this division, and West Ham will need every bit of attacking quality available if we’re serious about getting back into the Premier League.

Hopefully, Israel will make the sensible decision and only involve him against Austria if he is genuinely fit enough to play. We cannot afford another international break to leave us with a player who returns to east London carrying another injury.

#1991. How Liverpool feel about January recall for Ifeanyi Ndukwe amid Premier League loan enquiries

Liverpool are reportedly keen for Ifeanyi Ndukwe to continue his development on loan with Levante in Spain, despite the player now being eligible for a UK work permit.

The 18-year-old was a revelation for the Reds in pre-season but, at the time, he didn’t meet the criteria to play competitively in England and was subsequently dispatched to the LaLiga outfit for this season.

He’s continued to perform impressively for Los Azulgranas, and there were reports last month of his agents arranging to discuss the possibility of a January recall to Anfield.

According to Graeme Bailey for TEAMtalk, Liverpool are convinced that Ndukwe could break into their first-team setup next year and view him as ‘hugely important’ for their long-term plans.

Although he could theoretically be recalled in January, the Reds’ preference is for him to remain with Levante for the rest of his season and proceed with his development there.

That hasn’t stopped some Premier League clubs from enquiring about his availability for a loan move for the second half of the campaign to give him a first taste of English top-flight football.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Having had to wait until October for his first start for Levante, Ndukwe was then included from the first whistle in all six of their LaLiga games since the extended international break earlier in the autumn (Transfermarkt).

Luis Castro demonstrably has faith in the Austrian teenager, whose performances on loan have earned praise from the Spanish media, although the occasional error has served as a reminder that he’s still developing and will have off-days as part of that.

While Premier League exposure would be a quite informative barometer of the youngster’s readiness for the Liverpool first team, we’d be in favour of him continuing with Levante if he’s enjoying regular game-time there.

At the moment Ndukwe is featuring regularly in one of Europe’s foremost domestic leagues, and doing so with a club where media attention and scrutiny is comparatively sparse, thus keeping him away from the harshest of exposure.

He must be doing plenty right to have English top-flight clubs asking about taking him on loan in the winter. If that’s the case, then the current plan seems to be working, and we see no reason to deviate from that any time soon.

#1990. Real Madrid transfer news: Fabrizio Romano reveals truth behind Trent Alexander-Arnold to Liverpool links

By Saikat Mandal | 15 Nov 2026 20:31

Trent Alexander-Arnold has struggled to secure regular game time at Real Madrid this season, but a return to Liverpool in January appears to be out of the question.

The 28-year-old joined Madrid from Liverpool in the summer of 2025 and has made 43 appearances for the Spanish giants across all competitions.

However, the England international has managed just four starts in La Liga this season, with a further three appearances coming off the bench.

Alexander-Arnold has lost his place to Federico Valverde, with Jose Mourinho preferring to deploy the midfielder at right-back ahead of two recognised full-backs.

This has fuelled speculation that a potential return to Liverpool could be on the cards, but Fabrizio Romano has poured cold water on those rumours.

Romano has dismissed suggestions that all three parties are involved in discussions over a potential transfer.

Alexander-Arnold rose through Liverpool's academy to establish himself as one of the best right-backs in world football, although his departure from Anfield was not universally well received.

"Let’s immediately clarify one thing, there is zero ongoing between Trent Alexander-Arnold, Real Madrid and Liverpool, zero at all," said Romano to DAZN Football, as relayed by Roundtable.

The Italian journalist further emphasised that, while Alexander-Arnold retains enormous affection for the Reds, his priorities remain firmly in the Spanish capital.

"Trent obviously respects and loves the club but that’s it, it’s in the past. Trent is fully focused on Real Madrid and there is no contact or negotiation at all with Liverpool."

The England right-back would have been a fantastic addition to Andoni Iraola's system, but it appears unlikely that the Reds have any plans to bring him back.

Jeremie Frimpong has struggled to make a significant impact, but Ronald Araujo, who joined on loan from Barcelona, has done a decent job at right-back so far.

Conor Bradley remains sidelined through injury and is unlikely to return before the end of the year, but bringing in another right-back is not currently a top priority for Liverpool.

#1989. Origi recalls how Milan tenure turned sour: “We weren’t on the same page”

Divock Origi has discussed what went wrong during his time at AC Milan, from the injuries to the Rossoneri’s decision to exclude him.

Origi joined Milan after the Scudetto season, i.e. the summer of 2022, and the idea was that he would be able to alternate with Olivier Giroud. However, a couple of injuries made his start difficult and it only went downhill from there.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Despite making 36 appearances in his first season, he got just two goals and was thus sent out on loan for the next season, joining Nottingham Forest. One goal and one assist later, he returned to Milan, where it was quickly decided that he was no longer part of the project.

Instead of taking the opportunity to continue his career elsewhere, Origi decided to stay and train on his own. His hefty salary of €4m net (€5.24m gross) frustrated Milan and in December 2025, they finally got the striker to terminate his contract six months earlier than its expiration.

In short, it was a costly deal for Milan and for Origi, the move effectively killed his career. Speaking to the Belgian outlet HLN.be, as cited by MilanPress, the former striker explained what happened and why he then decided to retire (in the summer of 2026).

“At 27, my time at Liverpool was over. Sometimes you need to step out of your comfort zone and take on a new challenge. It’s the only way to grow as a person. AC Milan was a very interesting project.

“Paolo Maldini signed me and I felt he truly believed in me. It’s just that I got injured. Usually, I work on my preparation with my personal trainer, but this time it didn’t work. I lost much of my basic fitness; it was difficult.”

“I don’t take it personally. It was a professional decision. Was I happy about it? Obviously not. But can I understand it? Yes. I was left out of the squad for a while and wasn’t allowed to train with the first team.

“There was the option of joining the youth team. I can’t say too much about some things for contractual reasons… Let’s just say we weren’t on the same page about it. My experience helped me keep a clear head.

“I was convinced that if you have the right intentions, everything will work out for the best in the end.”

“I had options in football, but for me it was also a time when I was starting to think about my future away from the sport. Don’t get me wrong, I’ve always dedicated myself body and soul to football. It was my great passion, ” he stated.

#1987. Libya vs Tunisia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 15 Nov 2026 21:42

Tunisia will be looking to repair their faltering Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign when they travel to the 11 June Stadium in Tripoli to face Libya on Tuesday.

The Mediterranean Knights moved onto four points from three Group H matches with Friday's victory in Sfax, while the Eagles of Carthage sit bottom of the table with two points, still waiting for their first win of the campaign.

Libya opened their AFCON qualifying campaign with a 2-2 draw at home to Botswana, coming from two goals down through Marwan Al-Habashi's strike in the 87th minute and Ezoo El Mariamy's penalty deep into stoppage time.

They then suffered a 1-0 defeat away to Uganda, with Arnold Vula scoring the only goal, leaving them bottom of Group H before Friday's result moved them towards the top end of the table.

Coach Youssouph Dabo, the Senegalese who replaced Ali Cisse, had not won a competitive match in charge before Friday, making the victory all the more significant.

In Sfax, Libya took the lead after Ali Maaloul fouled Muaid Issa in the box, allowing Ali Youssef to convert from the penalty spot in the 44th minute, before Hamdou El Houni doubled their advantage on the counter-attack shortly after the hour mark.

The result marked Tunisia's heaviest home defeat in AFCON qualifying and the first time they had trailed by two goals on home soil in the competition.

It also ended more than 25 years without a two-goal home defeat in the qualifiers, prompting angry supporters to throw bottles and set off flares, while players and staff confronted referee Hamza El Fariq, who was subsequently escorted from the stadium.

Coach Mouine Chaabani has since apologised to supporters and admitted that the defeat was deserved, although Tunisia's decline stretches further back than the current qualifying campaign.

They lost all three matches at the 2026 World Cup, suffering defeats against Sweden (5-1), Japan (4-0) and the Netherlands (3-1), and have now gone nine games without a win, including September's draws against Uganda (1-1) and Botswana (2-2).

Before this campaign, Tunisia had qualified for each of the last 17 AFCON finals, the longest active streak of any nation, but with only one team besides co-hosts Uganda able to progress from Group H, they are running out of room for error.

Their record against Libya remains encouraging, however, as the visitors had won the previous six meetings before Friday's encounter, including a 5-2 away victory in 2021 and 3-0 and 1-0 wins in 2023.

Libya Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Tunisia Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Libya are expected to rely heavily on home-based players from clubs in Tripoli and Benghazi, with Youssouph Dabo naming a 27-man squad for the double-header.

Al Hilal Benghazi forward Ezoo El Mariamy is among the main attacking options, while Hamdou El Houni will be hoping to recover from the injury that forced him off during the first leg after scoring.

#1984. Niger vs Morocco - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 15 Nov 2026 21:42

Niger will be looking to respond to their heavy defeat in the first meeting when they face Morocco again in Tuesday's 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying fixture at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat.

The Mena suffered a 5-1 defeat in Casablanca on Friday, leaving them with three points from three Group A matches, while the Atlas Lions maintained their perfect start to the campaign and moved onto nine points after winning all three of their qualifiers.

Niger began their qualifying campaign with a 2-1 victory over Lesotho, but they were unable to build on that result when they travelled to face Gabon, suffering a 2-0 defeat in their second Group A fixture.

They then lost by the same scoreline to Algeria in an international friendly in October, before Friday's 5-1 defeat against Morocco extended their losing run to three matches across all competitions.

Their latest defeat was particularly frustrating because they managed to reduce the deficit to 2-1 before half-time through Mohamed Abdouramane's header, and were handed an opportunity to equalise shortly afterwards when a penalty was awarded for a handball by Noussair Mazraoui.

However, Yassine Bounou saved Ousseini Badamassi's spot kick, and Achraf Hakimi restored Morocco's two-goal advantage with a free kick in first-half stoppage time before the Atlas Lions added two more goals after the break.

The Mena have now conceded nine goals in their last three outings, including a 2-1 friendly defeat to Algeria, while scoring just twice during that period, leaving coach Nabil Neghiz with plenty to address after a difficult start to his tenure.

Morocco have now scored nine goals and conceded just once in their opening three qualifiers, having started the campaign with consecutive 2-0 victories over Gabon and Lesotho before Friday's emphatic win.

The Atlas Lions also drew 1-1 with Mali in a friendly in October, but their competitive form has been considerably more impressive, with the latest result extending their winning run in AFCON qualifying to nine matches.

Morocco have also won their last 16 home matches in major tournament qualifiers, covering both the Africa Cup of Nations and World Cup, marking their longest-ever winning streak on home soil in such fixtures.

With Tuesday's match also taking place in Morocco, with Rabat serving as Niger's adopted home for this fixture, Mohamed Ouahbi's side will remain on familiar territory and look to make further use of that advantage.

Morocco have consequently won the last three encounters between the sides by an aggregate score of 12-2 and boast a perfect record in this fixture, having won all seven meetings across all competitions.

Niger Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Morocco Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Niger named a 25-man squad for the November double-header, with nine players based in the domestic league and the rest drawn from clubs in Europe, Asia and other African countries.

Rahim Alhassane, who plays for Bologna, is expected to remain an important figure in defence, while Oumar Sako, Ali Mohamed, Daniel Sosah and experienced winger Tidjani Amadou Moutari are among the other notable selections.

Morocco are also working with the 26-man squad named by Ouahbi for the two matches, although several established internationals are missing, including Ismael Saibari, Azzedine Ounahi, Ayoub El Kaabi, Soufiane Rahimi, Chadi Riad and Hamza Igamane.

Youssef En-Nesyri returned to the squad and scored after coming off the bench in the first meeting, while Ayoub Oufkir marked his first senior call-up with a late goal, with both forwards now hoping to earn starting places after their contributions in Casablanca.

#1982. ‘They had different ideas’ – Rafa Benitez opens up about ‘difficult’ Hicks and Gillett era at LFC

Rafael Benitez has opened up about the ‘difficult’ time that he had at Liverpool during the damaging ownership era of Tom Hicks and George Gillett.

The American businessmen bought the Merseyside club in 2007 amid grandiose promises about a new stadium in Stanley Park (‘a spade in the ground within 60 days’, and all that), but they quickly became hugely unpopular figures among the fan base.

As the duo ultimately fell out with one another amid a period of civil war at the club, debts mounted to the extent that LFC was on the brink of administration in 2010 before they were ousted by a takeover from New England Sports Ventures (now Fenway Sports Group).

In an interview with The Athletic, Benitez was asked if he ever thought back to what could’ve been for Liverpool had it not been for the damaging ownership of Hicks and Gillett, throughout which time the Spaniard kept the club challenging for major silverware.

The former Reds boss reflected: “Yes, 100%. When Hicks and Gillett came, they changed the approach. All the things you did for the benefit of the club, they had different ideas. I realised, and the fans realised later, that something was wrong. They didn’t have experience of football.

“I remember speaking to Gillett once in London after we played Tottenham. He said: ‘We will give you money and then next season you’ll get us into the play-offs.’ I had to tell him there were no play-offs.

“They thought maybe: ‘Rafa is a threat.’ That period was difficult, but all I ever wanted was the best for the club.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Benitez’s final season at Liverpool in 2009/10 was a major disappointment, with the Reds expected to challenge for the title but slumping to a seventh-place finish, and there was a prevailing sentiment that the time was right for a change in the dugout.

However, as the extent of the damage done by Hicks and Gillett became clear in subsequent months and years, the latter part of the Spaniard’s managerial reign has come to be viewed in a much kinder light.

He was left with an impossible job of trying to achieve success on the pitch while all sorts of strife was going on in the background, slowly eating away at the club until John Henry rode to the rescue in October 2010.

Benitez’s time at Liverpool may have ended on a low ebb, but he remains a greatly appreciated figure among the fans for delivering Champions League glory in Istanbul and getting the Reds back to being a competitive force domestically and on the continent, even if the Premier League eluded him.

Had it not been for the incompetence of those at ownership level, who knows just how much more the Spaniard could’ve achieved at Anfield in the late 2000s and possibly into the 2010s?

#1980. West Ham Fans Asked to Unite in Memory of 19-Year-Old Supporter Luke

The loss of a young person reverberates far beyond their immediate family. Today, we are sharing Luke’s story in the hope of raising awareness, encouraging compassion, and supporting a tribute that means so much to those left behind.

Remembering Luke: A Young Life Gone Too Soon

At just 19 years old, Luke’s life was tragically cut short, leaving a family, circle of friends, and wider community struggling to come to terms with an unimaginable loss.

Known affectionately as “Lukey” and “Little Man” by those closest to him, Luke was a devoted West Ham United supporter and a loyal season ticket holder.

As they continue to navigate their grief, Luke’s family have made a simple but heartfelt request.

They are asking West Ham supporters attending the upcoming home fixture against Preston to join together in a minute of applause during the 19th minute of the match, marking the age at which Luke passed away.

The tribute is intended as a celebration of his life and a visible reminder that no family should feel alone during their darkest moments.

A shirt bearing Luke’s name will be placed on his seat in the stadium, providing a poignant symbol of the empty space left by his passing.

By sharing Luke’s story, we hope not only to support his family but also to encourage conversations around loss, grief, and the importance of supporting one another through difficult times.

C&H encourage anyone attending the match, or anyone who sees Luke’s story online, to help spread the word and support the planned tribute.

On the 19th minute, every clap will be a reminder that Luke’s life touched many people and that his memory continues to live on through his family, friends, and fellow supporters.

Our thoughts are with everyone who knew and loved Luke.

If this story resonates with you, please share it to help ensure Luke receives the tribute his family and friends are hoping for. Sometimes the smallest act of support can make the biggest difference.

England inflicted Spain's first defeat in 43 games on the World Cup winners with a sensational 3-2 victory in the Nations League, thus progressing to the quarter-finals as group winners.

Evidently learning their lessons from their gut-wrenching World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina, the Three Lions exploded out of the blocks in the Spanish capital, but Luis de la Fuente's backline weathered the early storm.

The world champions soon began to threaten James Trafford's goal too, but England got the reward their endeavours warranted on the stroke of the break, as Harry Kane dispatched a controversial penalty.

Neither the home nor away fans could then comprehend what they witnessed inside the opening 15 minutes of the second half, as Arsenal duo Ezri Konsa and Ben White incredibly extended England's lead, but the visitors were then forced to strap in for a nail-biting ending.

Barely moments after England's third went in, Elliot Anderson was sent off for a last-man foul and Mikel Oyarzabal dispatched the resulting penalty, before an Anthony Gordon error ended with Nico Williams cutting the arrears further.

However, the 10 men of England heroically held out in the dying embers to condemn Spain to their first loss since March 2024, and usurp the world and European champions at the top of League A Group 3.

#1978. West Ham player’s incredible injury statistic shows why he was the bargain of the summer

How managers and fitness conditioning teams must dread these international breaks – a player coming back with a serious injury picked up on duty for the national side must be every coaches’ fear. it seems a case of ‘so far so good’ for West Ham’s “international brigade” with no reports filtering through to Hammers HQ of new issues.

That does however leave the pre-existing condition: Manor Solomon’s frank admission to his national press will hardly reassure anyone at Rush Green. The winger has been struggling with a back injury and, according to sportwitness, this is neither a new issue nor one aggravated through too many games in the last window – which saw players asked to compete four times in twelve days for their nations:

“My back is something I’ve been dealing with for many years, ever since I was a teenager. I felt it during Saturday’s game; when I joined the national team, I felt fine, but by Tuesday, it had got worse, and I couldn’t train,” he said.

“Everyone knows how important the national team is to me and how hard it is for me to watch the team play while I’m not on the field. I hope I’ll be able to play on Tuesday.”

Facing a late fitness test, it seems Solomon is putting caution to one side in his desperation to be part of the Israel national team to take on Austria tomorrow.

Sadly, there is nothing new here, the old ‘club v country‘ debate in which domestic football (paying the players’ massive wages) gets a lesser priority from a player who will stop at nothing and go through the pain to play for his country.

Solomon looked like the deal of the decade after his first couple of outings, having joined West Ham for a mere £5 million up front.

More disclosures about his back issues and many and varied other problems – which have led him to sit out an incredible 860 days since the start of his career in 2018 ( according to sportwitness) make the price look more understandable by the week.

West Ham will have to cope with a player who has huge fitness issues but who doesn’t apparently, want to listen to his body, rather playing through the pain to represent his country. It’s not a combination that is likely preserve his longevity in the sport.

#1976. ‘We all fell in love with him’ – Hull coach shares what Lewis Koumas was like behind the scenes

A member of the coaching staff at Hull City has spoken very highly of what Lewis Koumas was like behind the scenes during his loan move at the MKM Stadium.

The Liverpool striker spent the second half of last season with the Tigers, playing a part in their promotion to the Premier League with three goals in 18 Championship appearances (including the play-offs).

He’s since become a fixed first-team player at Anfield, being handed five starts among his 14 appearances across all competitions and scoring in the Champions League victory over LASK in October.

Hull assistant coach Dean Holden spoke to The Redmen TV about how Koumas immediately won people over with his humility and hardworking attitude.

The 47-year-old said: “Within a week, everyone fell in love with him, from Stan on the door, the security guy, to the kitchen staff, kit men, the lot. We all fell in love with him.

“You know why? Just because he’s a real humble lad who just wants to be the best he can be and affects people around him in an energetic manner and just loves football.”

Holden went on to share anecdotes of Koumas being out on the training pitch along with Joe Gelhardt ’20 minutes out before everyone else is in the gym’, telling coaches not to ‘sugarcoat’ advice to him, and waiting patiently for his mother to collect him after he scored a late winner for Hull on his debut against Blackburn instead of ‘going out on the town and celebrating’.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

While we’re sure that the Liverpool youngster has been helped by sage advice from his father Jason, who graced the Premier League with West Brom and Wigan, the onus is still on him to put all of that bequeathed wisdom into action, and he’s most certainly doing that.

Andoni Iraola clearly has plenty of faith in the 21-year-old if he’s playing him regularly, even starting him against Manchester City (albeit that Alexander Isak wasn’t fit), and the young striker is repaying that trust with his performances on the pitch.

John Aldridge voiced his belief that the Wales international will ‘play for Liverpool for a long time‘, with Koumas standing out for his indefatigable pressing in the final third, which carries echoes of the beloved Bobby Firmino.

The stories shared by Holden testify to the tremendous attitude of the Reds youngster, who’s remained grounded and earned his place in the first-team squad to the extent that he’s nudged Federico Chiesa further down the pecking order.

We’re sure there’s still so much more to come from the Welshman, provided he can maintain the traits which have taken him this far already and (fingers crossed) avoid any major injury issues.

#1975. Tanzania vs Nigeria - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 15 Nov 2026 21:57, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 22:05

Africa Cup of Nations co-hosts Tanzania will be seeking their first win of the qualifiers when they welcome Nigeria to the Amaan Stadium on Tuesday.

While the match carries little significance for the hosts - already assured of a place at next year’s finals - the visitors remain fully focused, as a win would all but secure their own qualification.

No team in AFCON history has recorded more podium finishes (17) than Nigeria, who are regulars at the competition. After wins over Madagascar and Tanzania, either side of a 3-0 defeat to Guinea Bissau, the West Africans are on course to reach the tournament finals once again.

Despite missing several key attacking players, Eric Chelle’s men scored three goals in a competitive match for the first time since January, hinting at attacking depth across the squad, which is crucial given their overreliance on Victor Osimhen at times.

The Super Eagles have topped their AFCON qualifying group in each of the last four campaigns but currently trail Guinea Bissau by three points, so they cannot afford further slip-ups if they hope to finish as group winners.

Winless in their last four outings (D2, L2), Tuesday's visitors have been underwhelming away from home lately, so supporters travelling to Zanzibar City will be wary of further disappointment, with September’s heavy defeat in Bissau still fresh in the memory.

Converting just 10% of their chances so far, Nigeria need a much sharper edge in front of goal, especially given their ongoing defensive woes, having now gone six matches without a clean sheet since a 3-0 win over Jamaica in May.

While the result was inconsequential in the grand scheme, Tanzania were largely competitive in the first half of their 3-1 defeat to Nigeria, but a lacklustre second-half display set the stage for a second defeat in three outings.

Miguel Angel Gamondi’s men would have hoped the AFCON qualifiers might provide a preview of what to expect on their fifth appearance at the competition next year. However, based on recent results, hopes of a fairytale showing on home soil are quickly diminishing.

The Taifa Stars have now won just one of their last 16 matches across all competitions - a run that includes two meetings with Nigeria, who are unbeaten in seven previous encounters, winning five.

Tanzania are still awaiting their first competitive home victory since being awarded a 3-0 win over Congo in March 2025. As a result, some sections of the nation's faithful will approach this clash hoping for the best but expecting the worst.

A good start would help settle any nerves, but Tuesday’s hosts have conceded first in five of their last seven outings, and a repeat of that would be catastrophic, to say the least, given their current dry patch.

Tanzania Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Nigeria Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Ademola Lookman and Victor Osimhen are both ruled out with knee injuries, after Lookman was forced off just before half-time on Friday.

Igoh Ogbu (Achilles) and Samuel Chukwueze (thigh) are also unavailable for the visitors, who continue to monitor the fitness of Frank Onyeka.

Tolu Arokodare came off the bench to score twice last time out and could be rewarded with a start here as he looks to continue his impressive run of form.

Ibrahim Hamad is Tanzania’s most notable absentee due to a knock, following an impressive display at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium.

This should open the door for Charles M’Mombwa to come into the hosts’ starting XI, although Evastus Lukanima could also be considered.

Manula; Mligo, M’Mombwa, Mwamnyeto, Mnoga; Miroshi, Mkami, Msanga, Chilambo; Kachwele, Kibu

Nwabali; Aina, Bassey, Fredrick, Bewene; Yusuf, Iwobi, Ndidi, Nnadi; Arokodare, Adams

Despite the Super Eagles being far from full strength, anything less than a win here would be considered an underperformance.

With two leaky defences on display, goals are likely at both ends, but we expect the away side to come out on top when all is said and done.

Cody Gakpo has heaped praise on one of his Liverpool teammates who boasts ‘incredible football intelligence’ and is an ‘extraordinary player’.

The 27-year-old will come up against fellow Reds star Florian Wirtz tonight when Netherlands face Germany in the UEFA Nations League. The Dutchman is also set for a reunion with his former Anfield boss Jurgen Klopp, who takes charge of the home side in Berlin.

LFC’s number 7 has faced some stinging criticism among the British media since his £100m move from Bayer Leverkusen in June 2025, but he went into the international window off the back of scoring one goal and setting up another in the 3-1 win at Crystal Palace eight days ago.

Speaking to the media ahead of tonight’s match, Gakpo was keen to highlight the standout traits of his Liverpool teammate.

The Dutch forward said of Wirtz (via GOAL): “Regarding his situation at the club, I think in his last match he played amazingly. He scored a goal, provided an assist, and was very important for us.

“As a team, we know the quality he possesses; he shows it in every match and training session. He is an extraordinary player.

“Coming to Liverpool with an expensive transfer fee certainly makes the adaptation process in this league not easy for anyone, even for players who have had a 10-year career here.

“However, he has incredible football intelligence. The way he reads and dictates the pace of the game is very important to our style of play. We are very happy to have him.”

With nine goals and 15 assists in 64 games for the Reds so far, it’d be fair to expect a higher return from Wirtz considering his position on the pitch and the transfer fee that the club paid for him.

There have been other standout displays in recent weeks, including the game at Brentford when he created nine chances, and a terrific outing against Villarreal that he marked with a well-taken goal.

There are signs that Wirtz is now properly hitting his stride at Liverpool and primed to consistently turn in impactful performances, something he didn’t do often enough in his first season at Anfield.

Gakpo sees the 23-year-old at close quarters on a daily basis and is perfectly placed to speak about the German’s main qualities. On current form, our number 7 will be pivotal to our chances of success in the 2026/27 campaign.

#1972. Writing’s on the wall for West Ham stalwart’s international career

Time catches up with all of us, footballers just the same. Few are given much indication that the writing is on the wall, until suddenly that place which was automatically theirs is going to a younger, fitter, faster team mate – and then, suddenly, without a fanfare, almost always without even a ‘thank you’ –  it is over.

That, sadly, is likely to be the outcome for Czech stalwart and former captain Tomas Soucek who found himself an unused substitute last night after appearing for just five minutes in his countries’ previous game – during which Tornado Tom’s mistake in added time gifted Spain the injury time second goal in their 2 – 0 defeat of the Czechs.

A total of 93 appearances – 42 as captain – and nineteen goals is a pretty stellar international career and for Soucek to have fought his way back from such a bad injury at the World Cup last summer shows his fighting spirit.

You’d think it unlikely that Soucek will make the squad in the March window, after being virtually discarded for the two Nations League games just gone – both of which his Czech Republic side lost.

Hopefully it’ll give the veteran a little more gusto to complete the job and see his West Ham side over the line and promoted back to the Premier League – which would be a fitting swan song for Soucek who’d be 32 next season and probably a bit-part player if the Hammers make it back to the top tier.

#1971. Liverpool transfer news: Billionaire owner 'obsessed' with signing Virgil van Dijk for free as FSG contract decision nears

By Lewis Nolan | 15 Nov 2026 23:18

AC Milan owner Gerry Cardinale is obsessed with the idea of signing Liverpool defender Virgil van Dijk, the latest report has revealed.

The Reds' centre-back has so far enjoyed a strong season in England, helping the Merseysiders keep four clean sheets in their first 10 Premier League games.

However, fans are worried about the Dutchman's future given his contract is set to expire at the end of the campaign.

The 35-year-old has hinted that he would like to stay at Anfield, but there has seemingly been little movement regarding an extension.

Italian outlet Gazzetta dello Sport now claim that AC Milan's majority shareholder Cardinale is obsessed with the idea of signing Van Dijk.

Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG) have implemented a policy focused on rewarding younger stars at the club, while also moving on experienced players before they decline beyond the point of use.

There have been exceptions to those rules, with Van Dijk and Mohamed Salah both signing deals in 2025 following impressive seasons.

However, Salah struggled considerably in 2025-26 before leaving for free in the summer transfer window, and it would be understandable if the club were reluctant about handing another deal to a player in the twilight of their career.

Van Dijk's performances may be deserving of a contract offer, but FSG are unlikely to be swayed by any sentiment shared by fans, and they will instead make an emotionless judgement call in 2027.

Van Dijk is still one of the most physically imposing defenders in Europe, with the centre-back having won 75% of his duels in the Premier League this season.

Losing his experience would place significant pressure on Jeremy Jacquet next term, and the 21-year-old would benefit from spending more time without being the main man at the back for Andoni Iraola.

Liverpool are also likely to lose Alisson Becker and Joe Gomez for free in the summer, so ensuring there is someone at the club that has been through the peaks and troughs of life at Anfield would be sensible.

“When my father took me to try out for AC Milan, I liked playing goalkeeper, but luckily I ended up choosing to be a defender. I played football with my friends in the park and at the youth club: I didn’t feel like I was destined for success at all, and until the day I made my debut, I never thought I could reach the highest levels.

“My dad always told me that the most important thing is to have fun, because if you treat it only as a job, it loses its magic.”

“There’s one person in particular who believed in me and wanted me to play when I was 15: Nils Liedholm, then AC Milan’s coach. He loved showing his faith in young players, and once, during a break, he asked me whether I preferred to play on the right or left. I replied that it was obviously his choice, but it was a gesture that helped me a lot.”

As they say, one change and the rest is history. With Maldini, that was certainly the case.

#1965. “Don’t talk about it” – Liverpool star criticised for ‘stupid’ decision on international duty

One Liverpool player has been criticised for making a ‘stupid’ decision while representing his country during the international window.

Andoni Iraola was unsure whether Dominik Szoboszlai would partake in Hungary’s UEFA Nations League fixtures against Georgia and Northern Ireland after the midfielder sprained his knee in the Reds’ 3-1 win at Crystal Palace the weekend before last.

The 26-year-old did end up playing the entirety of his country’s 2-0 victory in Tbilisi on Saturday, although he admitted post-match that he felt a twinge during the warm-up and was close to pulling out before opting to play.

Liverpool-focused journalist David Lynch was critical of the midfielder for playing through the pain barrier to the potential detriment of his club, albeit with an acknowledgement that the Reds’ number 8 would feel duty-bound to represent his nation.

The reporter said on Anfield Index’s Media Matters podcast: “I think there’s no other way to describe this than stupid, really. He could have been a little bit smarter in terms of either not playing the game or, if you’re going to play through the pain in that way, maybe don’t talk about it.

“I don’t think Liverpool supporters are going to like it that you’re prioritising to such a degree. Playing for your country is a massive honour, and particularly when you are the captain, I absolutely understand that. I don’t want to play that down at all.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

This is a classic case of multiple parties having their own vested interests at heart. Hungary were obviously pushing for Szoboszlai to play, and he understandably wanted to come through for his country, whereas anyone of an LFC persuasion would much rather he sat it out.

If the midfielder comes through the match against Northern Ireland tomorrow night and is operating at (or close to) 100% for the Reds’ showdown against Manchester United next Sunday, then he’ll feel vindicated in his stance to continue playing.

However, by admitting that he wasn’t fully fit on Saturday, he’s left himself open to condemnation from Liverpool fans (and reporters, in Lynch’s case) who are justifiably asking why he took the risk of potentially aggravating an existing injury and curtailing his involvement for the club which employs him.

That sense of concern is heightened by Iraola’s team entering a frantic period of 11 matches in 40 days to end this calendar year, plus two more in the first five days of 2027. We can’t afford for Szoboszlai to be out of action amid that thankless fixture schedule.

We get that he didn’t want to let his country down unless he was completely unable to play, but he’s now placed added pressure on himself to be available over the coming weeks for Liverpool, and to deliver the kind of consistently top-class performances that he produced last season.

#1963. Sierra Leone vs Congo DR - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Ojele | 15 Nov 2026 23:31, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 23:32

Sierra Leone and Congo DR return to action in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers when they square off in the second of their Group E double-header at the Stade El Abdi on Tuesday.

While the Leopards will look to maintain their 100% record in the qualifiers and move another step closer to securing their place in next year’s continental showpiece, Sierra Leone head into the game under considerable pressure for a result, having lost their three matches so far.

Tasked with guiding Sierra Leone to a first Africa Cup of Nations tournament since 2022, French head coach Didier Gomes Da Rosa has failed to make his mark in the qualifiers, with the Lone Stars rooted to the bottom of Group E after the first half of the campaign.

While they showed signs of promise, Sierra Leone blew a two-goal lead in the group opener on September 24, when they fell to a 3-2 loss against Zimbabwe in Morocco, four days before suffering a 1-0 loss at the hands of Equatorial Guinea at the Stade Omnisport Ahmadou Ahidjo.

Sierra Leone were left with a mountain to climb in the qualifiers on Thursday, when they were beaten 3-1 by DR Congo, with Yoane Wissa, Samuel Moutoussamy and Watford man Edo Kayembe hitting the back of the net to fire the Leopards to all three points.

Having missed out on the 2025 AFCON after an underwhelming qualifying campaign that saw them finish third in Group G with five points from six matches, Sierra Leone are one of just six sides yet to pick up any points in the qualifiers, leaving them with little margin for further errors and in need of significant improvement.

Meanwhile, Congo DR kicked off their AFCON qualifying journey on a high, claiming a 2-0 victory over Equatorial Guinea on September 24, four days before edging out Zimbabwe 2-1 at the National Sports Stadium thanks to strikes from Wissa and Moutoussamy.

However, a break from competitive action saw the Leopards fail to win their subsequent two outings, losing 2-0 against Uganda on October 2, three days before playing out a 1-1 stalemate with the Cranes in the second of their friendly double-header at the FNB Stadium.

Congo DR returned to action in the AFCON qualifiers with a comprehensive team display against Sierra Leone on Thursday to remain one of just four nations with a 100% record in the campaign and move one step closer to sealing a third appearance in the continental tournament since missing out in 2021.

Sebastien Desabre’s men, who are currently 40th in the latest FIFA World Rankings, sit top of the Group E standings with nine points from a possible nine, five points above Zimbabwe and Equatorial Guinea, who sit level on four points after the first three games.

Congo DR will be backing themselves to maintain their perfect record on Tuesday when they take on an opposing side who have lost each of their previous four meetings, conceding 11 goals and scoring just twice since September 2014.

Sierra Leone Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Congo DR Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Sierra Leone came out unscathed against DR Congo on Thursday, and we expect Da Rosa to name a similar XI at the Stade El Abdi, with Alie Conteh and Elfsborg striker Momoh Kamara spearheading the attack.

Amidst their struggles at the defensive end of the pitch, Da Rosa could opt for a change in the back four, with Alpha Turay, who made his debut in June 2023, coming into the mix to form the centre-back pairing with Kilmarnock man Michael John Kamara.

As for DR Congo, APS Atromitos Athinon midfielder Moutoussamy was forced off injured midway through Thursday’s clash, and the 30-year-old is a doubt for Tuesday’s matchup.

Should he fail to shake off the injury, Lorient man Noah Mbamba, who made his debut on Thursday, will push for his first start in the Leopards’ colours, teaming up with Edo Kayembe and Sunderland man Noah Sadiki at the centre of the park.

Up top, Wissa made it three goals in three AFCON qualifying games with his opener against Sierra Leone on Thursday, and the Newcastle United striker should lead the attack once again, forming the front three with Nathanael Mbuku and Almeria winger Brian Cipenga.

With three games played already, Tuesday’s result will prove decisive in determining Sierra Leone’s qualifying fate, and we expect the Lone Stars to go all out at the Stade El Abdi as they look to get their campaign back on track.

Congo DR, who have shown their class in Group E so far, boast the quality and experience across the pitch to get the result here, and we are backing them to continue from where they left off on Thursday, extending their hot streak against Sierra Leone.

#1962. Can Scott Parker Fix What Nuno Couldn’t? West Ham News

Following the international break, Saturday’s clash with Preston North End feels like a pivotal moment in West Ham’s season. The Hammers desperately need to start climbing the table, and while promotion remains within reach, time is quickly becoming a factor.

Promotion from the Championship is not won on reputation alone. West Ham began the season as the bookmakers’ favourites for automatic promotion, but that tag has quietly disappeared.

The dismissal of Nuno and the appointment of Scott Parker signalled a fresh start, although our new manager has had limited time with the squad before the break. What already seems evident, however, is that West Ham’s struggles stem from structural issues rather than shortcomings of individual players.

Kretinsky was not prepared to back Espirito Santo any longer -his tactics and playing style were not working

Parker will be fully aware of the challenges facing his side. The Championship is a division where possession statistics mean very little unless they are backed up by purpose, intensity and results.

Goals have not been the problem. Defensive frailties have been the far greater concern. Playing  Morato at left back never looked convincing, and Saturday’s team selection will be fascinating. With Kilman unavailable due to suspension, Parker must decide whether to pair Mavropanos with Golambekis or Morato.

The absence of a prolific, out-and-out goalscorer has also raised questions. Joel Piroe was recruited to fill that role and, on paper, the logic was sound. He is a proven Championship striker. Four goals and two assists in 14 appearances suggest he is moving in the right direction, but when compared to the division’s leading scorer, Will Lankshear, who has 13 goals, the gap is impossible to ignore.

Ironically, West Ham are the Championship’s leading scorers with 37 goals. Encouragingly, those goals are coming from all areas of the pitch rather than relying on a single player. Yet, there is one player, Jarrod Bowen who has been central to that success, contributing seven goals and leading the league’s assist charts with seven in fifteen matches.

He will go if the club don’t secure promotion, an inevitable outcome should the club not succeed this season.

Perhaps the biggest challenge for West Ham, is psychological.

West Ham arrived in the Championship expecting results to come naturally. As fans we expected an automatic promotion place.

At times this season, West Ham have looked weighed down by expectation. Instead of playing with the confidence of promotion contenders, the team have often appeared nervous and overly cautious, afraid of making costly mistakes.

Scott Parker’s biggest task may not be tactical at all. He must build a mentality centred on resilience and belief rather than entitlement.

If he can transform West Ham into a side that is more aggressive, more robust and better suited to the harsh realities of Championship football, promotion is still very much achievable.

If he cannot, the club’s stay in the second tier could last far longer than anyone at the London Stadium ever imagined. Saturday could be the first real indication of which path they are heading down.

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

#1961. “Planning approval secured” : Stadium twist could change West Ham’s ownership plans

West Ham United’s window of opportunity to acquire their rented home for next to nothing appears to be fading. With £20 million of losses each year, the ground is a massive white elephant with the main tenant paying next to nothing for it’s bullet proof lease.

Former vice Chair Karren Brady, say what you like about her,  did at least negotiate the deal of the century giving West Ham a rock solid indestructible tenancy for generations to come. As the club were relegated, so the rent diminished leaving the owners to pick up the tab for West Ham’s failure on the pitch: An estimated £2.5 million each year is added to the tax payer burden thanks to the clause existing to reduce costs when West Ham dropped out of the Premier League.

Opportunities existed this summer, so we were told,  for the club to negotiate to buy the stadium, with suggestions that it would take £50 million for the deal to be done.

In the apparent lack of any take up by West Ham’s shareholders, the stadium owners have sought to bump up the former Olympic venue’s value in the meantime, by seeking to increase revenues through obtaining permission from Newham Council for a wider array of entertainment. According to London.stadium.com that effort has paid dividends:

Meaning the revenue which can be generated from the Stadium will be significantly higher, theoretically at least increasing its value and likely heading off West Ham’s options of acquiring it for next to nothing. Possibly.

West Ham’s London Stadium at night: There’ll be more events, louder music and bigger attendances – still won’t make a profit though. Just saying.

However the huge maintenance costs and temporary nature of the upper part of the structure means that even with consent for more events, bigger attendances and louder music, London Stadium is never going to become a lucrative, marketable venue in it’s current configuration.

Someone is going to have to spend hundreds of millions of pounds on fixing it: Like a giant pass-the-parcel game with a huge ticking time bomb of debt at the core of the fancy wrapping, neither West Ham nor the owners want to be left holding the bill when the music stops.

The difference is, the status quo favours the club, not the Greater London Authority who, as it stands, will find it pretty near impossible to turn a profit even with new approvals granted and new events lined up. And as every year passes, the need to spend big, big money on maintenance grows greater. In this instance, West Ham’s board biding their time and kicking it into the long grass for a few years yet is probably the shrewdest course of action. From the football club’s perspective.

According to City AM, the pair have reunited just seven months after departing West Ham, with Brady talking enthusiastically about the enormous commercial opportunities available in sport and entertainment.

I have to say, I find it absolutely incredible that Brady has any sort of influence or clout in a business focusing on sponsorship, hospitality and commercial strategy, considering the Baroness was vice-chair when West Ham recorded losses of £104.2m in their last published accounting period. And that’s before we get onto the rather awkward subject of the London Stadium.

West Ham’s accounts for the financial year ending May 2025 revealed a pre-tax loss of £104.2m, a remarkable turnaround from the previous year’s £57.2m profit.

Now, clearly, not every penny of that loss can be attributed to Karren Brady. Football finances are complicated, and player recruitment, wages, transfer dealings and league performance all have a significant impact.

But she was one of the most senior executives at the football club, and surely the financial performance of the business has to form part of any assessment of her commercial legacy.

Indeed, Claret & Hugh previously reported that Brady had even become directly involved in negotiating transfers during the January 2026 window.

I’ve questioned the timing of her departure before, particularly given the financial difficulties and footballing problems that were developing towards the end of her time at the club.

So forgive me if I’m not immediately convinced by the idea that the same leadership can now teach other organisations how to maximise their commercial potential.

But perhaps the biggest irony of all is the decision to launch an agency specialising in sponsorship when, after ten years at the London Stadium, West Ham and the stadium authorities collectively failed to secure a naming-rights partner for the former Olympic venue.

A Premier League football club, based in London, playing in a stadium with a capacity of more than 60,000, and after a decade nobody managed to get a naming-rights deal over the line.

That wasn’t solely Brady’s responsibility, of course. The London Legacy Development Corporation controlled the stadium’s commercial arrangements, and there were disagreements about the value of any potential deal.

In fact, Brady herself pressed the stadium authorities to pursue naming rights, and the London Assembly has documented correspondence in which she expressed West Ham’s willingness to help secure an agreement.

Nevertheless, the outcome remains the same.

As Claret & Hugh reported last year, the stadium operators were warning that a naming-rights agreement might not materialise until 2028 or beyond.

And in my previous article about the missing £4m sponsorship opportunity, I argued that the failure to secure a partner when the stadium first opened had allowed the London Stadium name to become so established that selling it now would be considerably more difficult.

That is hardly a ringing endorsement of the commercial arrangements surrounding West Ham’s move from Upton Park.

Brady told City AM that unlocking commercial opportunities required imagination, experience, relationships and the willingness to challenge convention.

Nathan Thompson, meanwhile, pointed to his experience negotiating commercial deals from different sides of the boardroom.

I’m sure both have considerable contacts within the business world, and there’s no doubt Brady has spent decades operating at decent levels of football administration.

But contacts and experience are one thing. Results are another.

Perhaps the venture will prove enormously successful. Perhaps they’ll secure the sort of sponsorship agreements that other sporting organisations have struggled to attract.

However, from a West Ham supporter’s perspective, it is difficult to look beyond the £104m loss, the club’s subsequent relegation and the decade-long failure to find a stadium naming-rights sponsor.

When somebody starts offering advice about how to unlock hundreds of millions of pounds in commercial value, I don’t think it’s unreasonable to ask why so much potential remained untapped at the football club they helped run for 16 years.

But hey, if all else fails the new company name of Brady Thompson does sound like excellent branding for a luxury soap should they wish to diversify.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

With over a decade of professional sports media experience, he is a frequent West Ham United analyst and contributor for Sky Sports News, BBC Football Focus, and BBC Radio 5 Live. He previously served as an official video and content creator for West Ham United FC during the club's tenure at Upton Park and featured in the official documentary commemorating the historic final game at the Boleyn Ground.

A lifelong Hammer since the legendary 10-0 victory over Bury, when he isn't providing daily match analysis on the Hammers Chat YouTube Channel or broadcasting on X (@GONZObignose), he can be found walking his dog and restoring classic pinball machines.

I remember walking toward stadium a few season when an ad for a skip hire company based in Ilford was displayed on the “largest wraparound screen” in Europe, which itself is still attached to a former Olympic stadium at the time hosting a match involving London-based club. That just about sums Brady up. Lots of talk, but ultimately unable to transform that talk into commercial revenues for the club, in the way that has happened at, say, Spurs. Globally-significant, easily-recognisable brand names were always out of Karren’s reach when she was with us but no doubt she knew where to turn if she ever needed to hire a skip. Hard to magine her new agency being inundated with offers.

I think that’s a tad unfair, haven’t I heard ‘deal of the century’ attributed to her!

Maybe she can approach West Ham to offer us the benefit of her wisdom

Lots of sarcasm intended. But imagine if that were actually to happen!

One has to wonder who will be their favourite client? Mr 40% per chance?

#1958. Singapore vs Brazil - prediction, team news, lineups

By Freddie Cotton | 15 Nov 2026 23:35

Singapore welcome Brazil to the Singapore National Stadium on Tuesday morning for their final international fixture of the calendar year.

In their previous outing, the Lions fell to a damning defeat against Paraguay, while Selecao conceded in additional time to lose 3-2 to Japan.

After a disappointing ASEAN Championship campaign, bowing out to Thailand in the semi-finals to deny themselves of a first crown in seven tournament editions, Singapore have endured a tough run of results to close out the calendar year.

Having fallen to defeat against Indonesia in their opening ASEAN Cup fixture in September, the Lions did well to bounce back with a narrow victory over Bangladesh, but after suffering a thumping 6-0 loss to Malaysia in their final group match, Gavin Lee’s men failed to qualify for the knockout stages.

Singapore have so far been unsuccessful in their attempt to bounce back during the current international break too, having endured a resounding 4-1 defeat against Paraguay on home soil last week, making it just the two victories in their previous eight outings.

However, facing Brazil for the very first time, the Lions have the opportunity to forget about their recent woes on Tuesday morning by claiming a historic victory against Selecao, in what would be the highest-ranked FIFA opposition the hosts have ever overcome.

Following last year’s mediocre World Cup qualification campaign, in which they finished fifth out of 10 South American nations and squeezing through to the competition finals, Brazil will undoubtedly be underwhelmed with how they performed in the summer’s tournament.

Despite concluding the group stage at the summit of the Group C table, pipping Morocco to top spot on goal difference, and edging past Japan in their first knockout fixture, Selecao’s tournament came to a premature end at the quarterfinal stage as they suffered a convincing 2-0 defeat to Norway.

Much like their opposition, Carlo Ancelotti’s men have failed to fight back from their tournament woes in recent friendlies too as although they have won two of their previous four matches, Brazil have faced much weaker opposition and head into Tuesday’s clash off the back of a disappointing defeat to Japan at the weekend.

If Selecao are to respond quickly, one of their biggest avenues for improvement is their defensive solidity, with Ancelotti’s side keeping just three clean sheets in their previous 14 games and conceding five goals over their latest three matches.

Having picked up no fresh injury concerns against Paraguay, Singapore head into Tuesday’s match with a predominantly fit squad, though the hosts are still without defender Nur Abdullah as the 25-year-old continues his recovery from an ACL injury.

After netting the equaliser on Friday, Ui-Young Song is almost certain to start in the Lions’ attack once again against Brazil, likely alongside fellow Lion City Sailors club teammates Farhan Zulkifli and Ilhan Fandi.

Following his red card in the dying stages of Saturday’s clash with Japan, 29-year-old forward Raphinha will be unavailable this week for Brazil, alongside Ancelotti, who will be absent from the sidelines having been sent off just moments later.

In the Barcelona winger’s absence, Ancelotti will be hoping that Vinicius Junior can continue his hot streak for Selecao, having netted both goals in the defeat to the Samurai Blue after a rocky patch to start the season for Real Madrid.

However, the visitors are missing multiple of their big hitters, with Gabriel Martinelli, Joao Pedro and Lucas Paqueta among those to be sidelined and unavailable for Brazil this week.

Mahbud; R.Stewart, Harun, Mahler, Baharudin; Nakamura, Shahiran; Zulkifli, H.Stewart, Song; Fandi

Bento; Wesley Franca, Cunha, Gabriel, Carlos Augusto; Guimaraes, Santos, Gomes; Estevao, Endrick, Vinicius Junior

With Selecao struggling to string a run of form together, Singapore can certainly be forgiven for having aspirations of a giant killing this week, especially on home soil.

However, despite their difficulties, we think Brazil will bounce straight back on Tuesday morning with a convincing victory at the Singapore National Stadium.

#1955. Liverpool favourite feared he ‘could have cost’ his country in hard-hitting self-assessment

Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet helped France to victory in the UEFA Nations League on Sunday, but he cut a frustrated figure after their 2-1 win over Turkiye.

The 21-year-old played the full 90 minutes in Bordeaux as Les Bleus finished top of Group A1 to ensure their place in the quarter-finals of the competition, his fourth international appearance after debuting against Belgium in late September.

The youngster has enjoyed an excellent start to his Reds career since moving from Rennes in the summer, but he survived an unenviable moment last night as he carelessly squandered possession in a dangerous area of the pitch before the offside flag came to his rescue.

Speaking after the win for France, Jacquet fronted up to that uncharacteristic error and was grateful that it was ultimately inconsequential for his country.

The Liverpool defender said (via via Made in Foot): “I perhaps preferred my first camp. Tonight, I could have cost the team dearly. Luckily, it was offside! These are little mistakes I need to cut out before I can be satisfied with my performances.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

As magnificent as Jacquet has been in recent weeks, that moment was a reminder that even he can have his lapses, following on from him turning his back for the free kick from which Fenerbahce scored their first goal in the 3-2 win over Liverpool earlier this month.

However, it says a lot about his mentality that he owned up to the mistake for France last night and still isn’t satisfied with his performances, despite his previous displays for Les Bleus drawing praise from some legendary figures of the past.

In the match against Turkiye, the 21-year-old was very tidy in possession and often sought to get his team on the front foot – as reflected below in the statistics from Sofascore – although he might be disappointed at his duel success rate.

Jacquet is still quite young and has had a sharp rise in his career over the past year, and as the stakes get higher in the stratospheric air of playing for Liverpool and France, he’ll learn that the scrutiny which comes with that territory is increasingly unforgiving.

However, his post-match comments after the win for Les Bleus reflect the standards that he expects of himself, and that ever-demanding attitude will serve him very well as he continues his upward trajectory.

One mistake doesn’t detract from what has been a fantastic year on a personal level for the defender, whose ceiling is incredibly high.

#1954. Kenya vs South Africa - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 15 Nov 2026 23:55

Kenya host South Africa in a 2027 Africa Cup of Nations Group D qualifier at Nyayo National Stadium in Nairobi on Tuesday.

The return leg arrives four days after substitute Ryan Ogam’s 90th-minute strike earned Harambee Stars a 2-2 draw in Soweto, a result that cut Pitso Mosimane’s lead at the top of the group to a single point over Guinea.

Kenya have taken two points from three Group D games, drawing 1-1 with Eritrea at Nyayo National Stadium, losing 1-0 away to Guinea and then drawing 2-2 in Soweto.

Qualification for the finals is already secured because Kenya co-host the tournament with Uganda and Tanzania, so only one non-host team from the group will advance and Benni McCarthy’s side are chasing a first win of the campaign rather than a place.

Kenya conceded in all three qualifiers, and the first leg followed the pattern: Amos Wanjala, who started in defensive midfield, sent a heavy backpass into his own net in the ninth minute, Michael Olunga levelled from the penalty spot in the 44th minute after Thabang Matuludi handled, and Ogam struck after Olwethu Makhanya was dispossessed.

McCarthy said his side struggled with South Africa’s full-backs until he moved to a back three early in the second half, with the wing-backs tasked with occupying them.

He has promised a more aggressive approach at home and pointed to Nairobi’s altitude and climate as conditions his players know and the visitors may not.

Olunga’s penalty was his 35th goal for Kenya, level with William Ouma as the national record scorer, and one more would make him the outright leader less than a week after returning from roughly five months out with a pelvic injury that required surgery in Paris.

Ogam, who plays for RFC Liege, has scored two of Kenya’s three group goals, an 87th-minute equaliser against Eritrea and the late leveller in Soweto, the first open-play goal Kenya have scored against South Africa.

McCarthy, born in Cape Town and South Africa’s record international scorer with 31 goals, was facing his native country as a head coach in a competitive match for the first time, and President William Ruto has urged supporters to fill Nyayo National Stadium for the return.

South Africa arrive in Nairobi with seven points from three games, one ahead of Guinea, after beating Guinea 2-1 and Eritrea 5-0 before the draw in Soweto.

The 2-2 result was the first time Bafana Bafana dropped points since Mosimane returned as head coach, and they led twice without being able to hold on.

Relebohile Mofokeng of Union Saint-Gilloise now has three qualifying goals, two in the 5-0 win over Eritrea and the 77th-minute finish in Soweto that followed a pass from substitute Lyle Foster.

Mosimane’s side have scored nine and conceded three in three games, and both Kenya goals in Soweto came from defensive lapses, with Matuludi’s handball giving away the penalty and Makhanya failing to clear before Ogam won the ball.

Mbekezeli Mbokazi, who missed the wins over Guinea and Eritrea with a thigh injury, is available again after being left out of the first-leg XI, and Makhanya is the obvious player to make way.

South Africa have never lost to Kenya in normal time, with three wins and a 1-1 draw in four previous friendlies, although Kenya won the 2002 penalty shootout that followed that draw.

Mosimane said the squad took the first available flight to Nairobi, leaving at 01:00 on Saturday and landing at around 06:00, and that no player reported fatigue when the group trained on Sunday.

Kenya Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

South Africa Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Kenya have no suspensions reported, and Olunga and defender Eric Ouma are back after long injury layoffs, with Ouma used as a substitute in Soweto.

Wrexham defender Zak Vyner was left out of the first leg because of a paperwork problem, and McCarthy said he was hopeful that it would be resolved in time for Tuesday, which would allow the uncapped 29-year-old to make his debut.

Olunga was replaced by Micah Obiero in the second half in Soweto, so the captain’s match fitness is the main selection question, while Ogam is pushing for a start after coming off the bench to score.

Byrne Odhiambo, Frank Odhiambo, Sylvester Owino, Abud Omar and Rooney Onyango all started in the first leg, and McCarthy used Wanjala in midfield before moving him into a back three.

For South Africa, Mosimane has the full squad available, with no suspensions, although centre-backs Ime Okon and Makhanya each carry one yellow card and a second caution would rule them out of their next qualifier.

Goalkeeper Ronwen Williams and midfielder Teboho Mokoena were fitness doubts after missing Mamelodi Sundowns matches, yet both started in Soweto, while Thapelo Maseko missed the squad through injury and Themba Zwane and Nkosinathi Sibisi were left out.

Williams will want to bounce back after Olunga sent him the wrong way from the spot, a penalty McCarthy highlighted because the goalkeeper is regarded as one of the best penalty stoppers in Africa.

Up front, Oswin Appollis, Tshepang Moremi and Iqraam Rayners started in Soweto, with Foster and Puso Dithejane replacing Moremi and Rayners in the second half and lifting the side.

B. Odhiambo; Wanjala, F. Odhiambo, Owino; Omar, Tera, J. Ochieng, R. Onyango; Wilson, Olunga, Ogam

Williams; Matuludi, Mbokazi, Okon, Modiba; Sithole, Mokoena; Appollis, Mofokeng, Moremi; Foster

South Africa have the sharper attack, with nine goals in three games against Kenya’s three, and Mofokeng, Appollis and Moremi should find space on the flanks if McCarthy follows through on his promise to push higher up the pitch.

Kenya’s counter-argument is strong, because the back-three adjustment worked in Soweto, Nairobi’s altitude is a real factor, and Olunga needs one goal to hold the national scoring record outright.

Even so, Kenya have conceded in all three qualifiers and have not kept a clean sheet, while Mosimane can restore Mbokazi to fix the problem that cost his side two points.

A team that has twice squandered a lead should respond with more control, and South Africa’s depth up front should be enough to take a narrow win, with Olunga or Ogam likely to give Kenya a consolation.

“We’ve also found the right position for Flo. It helps that he’s so vocal. He’s the first pressing player, can press two players without getting tired.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Klopp’s lofty praise of Wirtz comes just after the 23-year-old’s Liverpool teammate Cody Gakpo hailed his ‘incredible football intelligence‘, and the Reds’ number 7 has been busy confounding his doubters in recent weeks.

He’s been subjected to some heavy criticism since his £100m move from Bayer Leverkusen in June 2025, with Jamie Carragher even calling for him to be dropped from the starting XI, but right now he’s one of the first names on the team sheet for club and country.

In addition to his two goals against Netherlands on Monday, he won three duels, completed 88% of his passes and recorded a 100% dribble success rate (Sofascore), delivering a fine performance throughout the night.

Klopp has worked with several world-class players throughout his managerial career, so for Wirtz to leave him ‘shocked’ with his quality just shows how much talent the Liverpool playmaker possesses.

The coach’s comment about the 23-year-old being vocal are also noteworthy – could he develop into a potential future captain for the Reds, provided he stays at Anfield for the long-term?

Our number 7 has copped his share of flak since coming to England, but right now he’s undoubtedly a crucial figure for club and country.

De Winter possesses immense speed, and the 24-year-old is far more mobile then any of United's current options at the back.
