#1948. Japan vs Paraguay - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 16 Nov 2026 00:29, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 03:27

Japan and Paraguay will conclude their respective 2026 schedules when they face off in Tuesday's friendly in Singapore.

The Samurai Blue pulled off a thrilling win over Brazil last time out, while Paraguay cruised to a commanding victory over Singapore in their most recent outing.

Japan head into Tuesday's fixture in fine form, having lost just one of their previous 16 internationals.

Their only defeat in that period came in the Round of 32 tie against Brazil at the 2026 World Cup, which saw them spurn a leading position in a narrow 2-1 defeat.

After conceding a late winner in that contest, Hajime Moriyasu's side managed to exact an element of revenge with a stoppage-time winner of their own in Saturday's friendly against Brazil.

The Samurai Blue looked to have wasted another strong position after Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura saw their efforts cancelled out by a Vinicius Junior brace, before Coventry City's Tatsuhiro Sakamoto turned the game back in Japan's favour with a 91st-minute goal.

Sakamoto's effort made it two wins in Japan's last three head-to-head meetings with Brazil, while making it five games without defeat since their World Cup elimination.

Japan should fancy their chances of extending their unbeaten run with a win, having won four of their previous five meetings with Paraguay (D1) since losing on penalties in the last 16 of the 2010 World Cup.

After eventually being eliminated in the quarter-finals in 2010, Paraguay had to wait 16 years until their next appearance in football's biggest tournament.

La Albirroja certainly made an impact at the 2026 World Cup, advancing to the knockout rounds before eliminating Germany on penalties in the Round of 32.

However, their run ultimately came to an end in a feisty last-16 clash against France, with Kylian Mbappe's 70th-minute penalty proving decisive as Paraguay fell to a narrow 1-0 loss.

Gustavo Alfaro's side have since made a positive return to action with three consecutive wins against Bolivia, Colombia and Singapore.

Gustavo Caballero netted a brace as Paraguay cruised to a 4-1 success in their most recent outing against Singapore, representing just the third time La Albirroja have scored two or more goals in 2026.

Their strength has ultimately been at the opposite end of the pitch, having conceded more than one goal in just two of their 11 games in the current calendar year.

Japan have announced that Daichi Kamada has been allowed to return to Crystal Palace after playing 72 minutes in the win over Brazil.

Ko Itakura, Yukinari Sugawara and Kaishu Sano are among those who could start if Moriyasu opts to rotate his side.

Sakamoto, Takumi Minamino and Koki Ogawa could come in to freshen up Japan's attack for Tuesday's friendly.

As for Paraguay, Alfaro is expected to make wholesale changes after naming an experimental XI for the win over Singapore.

Juan Jose Caceres, Gustavo Gomez and Omar Alderete are likely to come into the back four for Paraguay's final outing of 2026.

Diego Gomez, Miguel Almiron and Julio Enciso are also among those who are expected to start against Japan.

Suzuki; Sugawara, Seko, Itakura, Ito; Ka Sano, Tanaka; Sakamoto, Minamino, Nakamura; Ogawa

Gill, Caceres, G. Gomez, Alderete, Maidana; Cuenca, Galarza, D. Gomez, Almiron; Benitez, Enciso

Japan will be full of confidence after pulling off a notable win over Brazil, and while we think they will claim another victory on Tuesday, we believe the scoreline will be close against a Paraguay team that is usually a tough side to break down.

#1947. ‘I am sure…’ – John Aldridge sets Alexander Isak goal tally target for rest of the season

John Aldridge has specified what he feels is a realistic goal tally target for Alexander Isak to try and hit for Liverpool this season.

After an injury-ravaged debut campaign at Anfield in which he netted just four times in 22 appearances, the Swedish marksman has doubled that return in his first 14 outings in 2026/27, scoring seven times in nine Premier League games (Transfermarkt).

Having cost a club-record fee of £125m to sign from Newcastle in the summer of 2025, the 27-year-old has been repaying that outlay with his consistent goalscoring form since August, accounting for 50% of the Reds’ top-flight goal tally for the season so far.

In his latest column for the Liverpool Echo, Aldridge voiced his confidence in Isak to maintain the excellent form that he’s been showing since the start of the campaign.

The former Reds striker wrote: ‘If Liverpool are to have a successful season, then a lot will rest on the goals of Alexander Isak.

‘Now up to eight for the season, the striker just needs to keep getting in the positions and if the chances come, like they have been doing, then more often than not you expect him to finish them off.’

In terms of a goal target for the campaign, Aldridge specified: ‘Having scored eight by this point of the season, I am sure he will be targeting the 20-25-goal tally now.’

(Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Provided that Isak avoids a recurrence of the injury issues which plagued him last term and extrapolates his current form over a full campaign, there’s no reason why he can’t match Aldridge’s target by the end of May.

With eight goals in 14 matches up to this point, maintaining that return would see Liverpool’s number 9 reach the 20-goal mark in 35 games, and get to 25 goals inside 44 appearances.

As it stands, the Reds will play a bare minimum of 50 matches across the campaign – realistically that number will be closer to 55-60 with progression in the Champions League and domestic cups.

With that in mind, it’s not inconceivable that Isak could get close to 30 goals if he stays fit and in form, although he could be rotated more frequently once Hugo Ekitike returns from injury over the winter, as is currently projected.

Liverpool’s greatest ever goalscorer in Ian Rush rightly said that finding the net is ‘all that matters’ for a centre-forward, and the Sweden international has been doing that in abundance this season.

Barring a cruel twist of fate, we’re sure that the 27-year-old will top the 2o-goal mark by the end of the campaign. At this rate, he could hit it by the end of February.

#1945. Liberia vs Cape Verde - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 16 Nov 2026 00:32

Bottom-placed Liberia host Cape Verde in a Group K fixture of 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying at the Samuel Kanyon Doe Sports Complex in Monrovia on Tuesday.

The first leg in Praia on November 13 finished 4-2 to Cape Verde, which lifted the Blue Sharks to three points in third place in a group where only the top two qualify, left Liberia on zero, and kept Mali on nine points and Rwanda on six above them.

The Lone Stars sit bottom of Group K with no points from three matches, having scored three goals and conceded eight, a goal difference of -5 that leaves them six points behind second-placed Rwanda with nine still available.

Mohammed Adil Erradi, the Belgian-Moroccan appointed on a three-year contract on May 18, has yet to win a competitive match as Liberia coach, and a group calling itself the Concerned Stakeholders for Liberian Football Development demanded his dismissal on October 9, according to the Liberian Observer, citing a salary budgeted at US$98,450 a year.

The campaign opened with a 3-1 defeat in Kigali on September 25, where Sylvanus Nimely scored the only Liberian goal, and four days later Mali won 1-0 at this ground through Martial Tia’s 79th-minute strike after goalkeeper Tommy Songo pulled out of the starting line-up during the warm-up.

In Praia on November 13 Liberia trailed 3-1 after 43 minutes, with Franklin Nyenetue’s 36th-minute equaliser cancelled out two minutes later by a corner-kick header from Dje Tavares, before Ayouba Kosiah converted a stoppage-time penalty to set the final score at 4-2.

Liberia’s back three of Jamal Arago, Sampson Dweh and Emmanuel Fully conceded to a scramble in their own box, a corner and a marking lapse in the first leg, and the defence has now shipped eight goals in three qualifiers, an average of 2.67 per match.

The head-to-head record leans away from the hosts, as Liberia have lost their last three meetings with Cape Verde (2-1 in Accra on October 7, 2021, 1-0 in Mindelo on October 10, 2021, and 4-2 on November 13), although both of their wins in the series came in Monrovia, 3-0 in July 2000 and 1-0 on June 5, 2011.

A post shared by Liberia Men's National Teams (@lbr_lonestar)

Cape Verde arrive third in Group K on three points with a goal difference of -1 (six scored, seven conceded), and a win in Monrovia would take them to six, level with the total currently held by second-placed Rwanda, who host Mali in Kigali at the same 7pm GMT kick-off.

The Blue Sharks drew all three of their World Cup group matches in June (0-0 against Spain, 2-2 against Uruguay and 0-0 against Saudi Arabia) to reach the Round of 32 on their tournament debut, where Argentina beat them 3-2 after extra time on July 3, a 111th-minute own goal from Diney Borges settling it after Deroy Duarte and Sidny Lopes Cabral had pulled Cape Verde level twice.

Bubista then left to coach Moroccan club RS Berkane, and Humberto Bettencourt, his assistant for six years, was promoted on August 19, with his first two qualifiers producing a 3-1 defeat at Mali on September 25 and a 2-1 home defeat to Rwanda on September 29.

Those results extended a winless run to six matches, counting the World Cup (three draws and three defeats), which ended in Praia when Ayoni Santos, Dje Tavares, Dailon Livramento and substitute Derensili Sanches Fernandes scored in the 4-2 win, Bettencourt’s first victory in charge.

Cape Verde have conceded in all three of their qualifiers, seven goals at 2.33 per match, compared with five conceded across four World Cup matches, two of which were clean sheets against Spain and Saudi Arabia.

Bettencourt brought in six players for the double-header, among them David Moreira, Yuran Fernandes, Leandro Andrade, Ieltsin Camoes and Sanches Fernandes, and three of the four scorers in Praia (Santos, Tavares and Sanches Fernandes) were finding the net for the senior side for the first time.

Liberia Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Cape Verde Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Liberia captain Oscar Dorley, the Al-Taawoun midfielder, is out with a hamstring injury and was left out of Erradi’s 24-man squad, while goalkeeper Derrick Julu of Niger Tornadoes was recalled to replace Songo, who has not featured since withdrawing from the Mali line-up on September 29.

Julu replaced Ashley Williams at half time in Praia, and Erradi said afterwards that Williams, who had played well against Mali, was not at his best, which points to Julu starting in goal on Tuesday.

Nyenetue, who plays for Ranheim, scored the equaliser in Praia and was replaced by William Gibson after 64 minutes with no injury reported.

Without Dorley, Nohan Kenneh and Solomon Tweh are the likeliest holding pairing in a four-man midfield that also used Edward Ledlum and Divine Teah of Slavia Prague, with Sampson Dweh of Viktoria Plzen anchoring the back three.

For the visitors, defender Wagner Pina, who had joined the training camp in Portugal, did not travel to Cape Verde for the first leg, and Bettencourt wished him a quick recovery.

The 26-man squad named on November 4 includes Vozinha, 40, defenders Logan Costa and Lopes Cabral, midfielder Jamiro Monteiro and 36-year-old captain Ryan Mendes, although Lopes Cabral was replaced at half time in Praia by Steven Moreira and the reason has not been given.

Bettencourt could keep the 4-1-4-1 that scored four in Praia, with Deroy Duarte shielding the back four, and he used all five substitutions there (Moreira, Monteiro, Laros Duarte, Sanches Fernandes and Camoes), which leaves a bench that is already familiar with the plan.

Julu; Fully, Dweh, Jamal, Nimely; Ledlum, Tweh, Kenneh, Nyenetue; Teah, Kosiah

Vozinha; J. Paulo, Diney, Costa, L. Cabral; D. Duarte; Mendes, Tavares, Santos, Varela; Livramento

The first leg showed where this tie will be decided, as Liberia conceded to a scramble in their own box, a corner and a marking lapse inside 43 minutes, and with Dorley absent and Erradi having already changed goalkeepers at half time, he has fewer ways to repair that in four days than Bettencourt has to exploit it again.

Liberia deserve credit for scoring twice in Praia and for restricting Mali to a 79th-minute winner on the synthetic surface at this ground, and both of their wins over Cape Verde came in Monrovia, but the later of them is 15 years old and Cape Verde’s own record of conceding in every qualifier gives the hosts a route to one goal, which is why 1-2 is a better call than a repeat of the four-goal margin.

A Cape Verde win would lift them to six points, which only equals Rwanda’s tally if the Amavubi lose to Mali in Kigali on the same evening, so Bettencourt’s side cannot treat the second leg as a formality.

#1943. Jordan vs Australia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Saikat Mandal | 16 Nov 2026 00:33, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 08:05

Jordan and Australia will face off in a rare November international friendly at Suheim Bin Hamad Stadium in Doha on Tuesday.

The home side are striving for consistency following their group-stage exit from the 2026 World Cup, while Australia will be looking to make it back-to-back away victories.

Jordan may have fallen short of the group-stage hurdle at their first-ever World Cup, but they still produced some memorable moments for their supporters.

Despite suffering a 3-1 defeat to Austria in their opening game, Ali Olwan's stunning strike remains fresh in the memory.

Jordan failed to win either of their remaining matches against Algeria and Argentina, but they showed no shortage of fighting spirit before their World Cup campaign came to an end.

Badou Zaki's side are now without a win in their last 10 matches and have recorded two draws since the tournament.

The Chivalrous Ones played out a 1-1 draw against Syria in their first match after the World Cup in September before being held to a goalless stalemate by Venezuela in October, extending their winless run through two underwhelming friendlies.

In contrast, Australia enjoyed a memorable tournament, reaching the knockout stages despite being drawn in a difficult group.

Tony Popovic's side stunned many with a 2-0 victory over a strong Turkey outfit in their opening match.

They subsequently lost 2-0 to the USA, but a goalless draw was enough to secure their passage into the knockout rounds, where they suffered a 4-2 penalty shootout defeat to Egypt after the match finished 1-1 in normal time.

Australia faced Brazil twice in international friendlies after the World Cup, drawing 1-1 in the first encounter before losing 4-2 in the return fixture.

However, they head into this contest with renewed confidence after thrashing Qatar 3-0 earlier this week, with all three goals arriving in the first half.

Zaki has a fully fit squad at his disposal, and it will be interesting to see which combination he opts for.

Abdallah Al-Fakhouri could retain his place in goal, although Alec Samir featured in the 1-1 draw against Syria.

World Cup hero Mousa Al-Tamari is expected to lead the attack alongside Olwan and veteran forward Mahmoud Al-Mardi.

Australia, meanwhile, are missing several key players, with Cameron Burgess ruled out by a cruciate ligament injury and Jordan Bos also sidelined with a knee problem.

The Socceroos are also without skipper Mathew Ryan and fellow veterans Jackson Irvine and Milos Degenek, plus midfielder Aiden O'Neill, but it unclear whether they made themselves unavailable for safety reasons.

Diesel Herrington, Thomas Waddingham and Sam Klein are new call-ups, while striker Kusini Yengi joins brother Tete Yengi, while goalkeepers Joe Gauci and Tom Glover have been recalled.

The Eagles only required a draw against Romania last time out to secure a place in an inter-division showdown, but they were beaten 2-1 in Bucharest on Saturday.

Knowing that victory for their rivals could force them into the automatic relegation spot, Poland will be fearing a clash against in-form Sweden, especially after losing three of their last four outings.

However, the hosts will take heart from the fact they are unbeaten on home soil during this group stage, having drawn 0-0 with Bosnia-Herzegovina on September 25, before thrashing Romania 6-0 a week later.

Meanwhile, Graham Potter's Sweden are yet to taste defeat in Group B4, and are set to play League A football next term following an excellent campaign.

The Blue and Yellow held on to beat Bosnia-Herzegovina 3-2 on Saturday, racing into a three-goal lead courtesy of a fifth-minute opener from Borussia Dortmund's Daniel Svensson and a pair of penalties from Arsenal's Viktor Gyokeres, but conceded twice in a tense second half.

That performance fits Sweden's pattern, considering they have scored in the first 20 minutes during six of their last seven Nations League clashes, while 13 of their past 15 matches have seen both sides find the back of the net.

Regardless, securing their fourth win in five games has Potter's men top of the group with 13 points, five clear of the second-placed Dragons and nine above third-placed Poland.

The Blue and Yellow may no longer be under pressure, but they will be keen to end on a positive note, and having won eight of their last nine meetings with Poland, supporters will be looking forward to another triumph on Tuesday.

Poland will be without Porto centre-back Jakub Kiwior, who is suspended due to accumulating yellow cards, while Aston Villa right-back Matty Cash is a doubt with a leg problem and goalkeeper Kamil Grabara is sidelined with a cruciate ligament injury.

In their absence, Kacper Potulski could be joined by Tomasz Kedziora at the heart of the hosts' defence, flanked by Arkadiusz Pyrka and Oskar Kubiak at full-back in front of shot-stopper Bartlomiej Dragowski.

Elsewhere, Inter Milan midfielder Piotr Zielinski is unavailable due to illness, though Sebastian Szymanski and Wiktor Nowak should be on hand to start in the centre of the park.

As for Sweden, they are missing Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Lucas Bergvall (knee) and Lech Poznan winger Patrik Walemark (muscle).

With that in mind, expect to see Fulham's Hugo Larsson and Brighton and Hove Albion's Yasin Ayari line up in midfield, while Anthony Elanga and Sebastian Nanasi provide width.

Liverpool striker Alexander Isak will partner Viktor Gyokeres up top on Tuesday, with the latter hoping to add to his brace from last time out.

Dragowski; Pyrka, Potulski, Kedziora, Kubiak; Regula, Szymanski, Nowak, Zalewski; Lewandowski, Swiderski

Johansson; Svensson, Lagerbielke, Lindelof, Gudmundsson; Elanga, Larsson, Ayari, Nanasi; Gyokeres, Isak

Poland are sure to be feeling the pressure from Romania on Tuesday, and they will be keen to confirm their place in the playoffs.

However, Sweden have dominated the head-to-head clashes between these nations, and are likely to continue that trend in midweek.

#1934. Bosnia-Herzegovina vs Romania - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 16 Nov 2026 02:26

Romania will be battling for a chance at avoiding relegation from UEFA Nations League B on Tuesday, when they travel to face Bosnia-Herzegovina at Stadion Bilino Polje.

The Dragons have already secured second in Group B4, and are up against a Tricolorii team that need to win.

Sergej Barbarez's Bosnia-Herzegovina will be hoping to end their group stage on a high note after nailing down a spot in the League A/B playoffs.

The Dragons were downed 3-2 by group winners Sweden on Saturday, conceding three first-half goals before falling agonisingly short of a comeback with two strikes of their own in the second period.

In fairness to Barbarez's side, that loss was their first of this Nations League campaign following two draws and two wins, including a 4-2 triumph over Tuesday's opponents on September 28.

Heading into this clash, Bosnia-Herzegovina are second with eight points - five behind Sweden but four clear of third-placed Poland - and securing the runners-up spot has presented the Dragons with a shot at promotion to League A.

Another victory in midweek could give the team a boost ahead of their playoff, and fans will be expecting a positive result, given that Barbarez's men have not suffered back-to-back defeats since November 2024.

Meanwhile, Gheorghe Hagi's Romania have delivered a dire campaign so far, but escaping with all three points on Saturday has given them a glimmer of hope.

The Tricolorii lost each of their first four Nations League fixtures this term, conceding 13 goals while scoring just three in the process, and seemed doomed to relegation to League C.

However, a shock 2-1 victory over Poland last time out has placed Group B4's bottom side just one point behind the third-placed Eagles in the League B/C playoff spot.

Due to their 6-0 thrashing by Poland on October 2, Romania must beat Bosnia-Herzegovina while hoping that their rivals drop points to Sweden in order to avoid automatic demotion.

That being said, the Tricolorii have not come out on top in any of their eight away matches since hammering San Marino 5-1 in March 2025, losing six times and drawing twice.

Bosnia-Herzegovina have doubts about the readiness of striker Haris Tabakovic, who was forced off just 39 minutes into the clash against Sweden due to a knee injury.

If the Red Bull Salzburg man is unavailable, then Ermedin Demirovic could be joined by Ermin Mahmic up front on Tuesday, supported from out wide by Esmir Bajraktarevic and Kerim Alajbegovic.

At the opposite end of the pitch, centre-back Dennis Hadzikadunic is sidelined with a muscle injury, so Nikola Katic and Stjepan Radeljic should start at the heart of Barbarez's defence.

As for Romania, they are missing midfielder Tudor Baluta, who is suspended for accumulating yellow cards, so Alexandru Cicaldau, Vladimir Screciu and Vlad Dragomir are likely to operate in the centre of the park.

Elsewhere, Florinel Coman and Dennis Man look set to lead the line once again on Tuesday, aided in attack by Alanyaspor's Ianis Hagi.

Bosnia-Herzegovina possible starting lineup:

Zlomislic; Dedic, Katic, Radeljic, Kolasinac; Bajraktarevic, Basic, Gigovic, Alajbegovic; Mahmic, Demirovic

Hindrich; Ratiu, Coubis, Dragusin, Eissat; Cicaldau, Screciu, Dragomir; Hagi; Coman, Man

Bosnia-Herzegovina may have lost to Sweden at the weekend, but they have proven resilient across this Nations League campaign and will be seen as overwhelming favourites on Tuesday.

Romania have struggled in League B, and given their dire away form - not to mention their four defeats this term - it would be surprising to see the visitors avoid another loss.

#1933. Report: How Ronald Araujo, Barcelona and Liverpool feel about prospective permanent transfer

Reports from Spain have hinted that there’s a strong chance of Ronald Araujo signing for Liverpool permanently in 2027.

The Uruguayan defender is on loan at Anfield from Barcelona for this season, with the deal including a purchase option reportedly worth £47m.

The 27-year-old has been one of the Reds’ standout players in the first three months of the campaign, making the right-back berth his own despite playing most of his career at centre-back, and it’s been reported that he and his family are very happy and comfortable on Merseyside.

According to Marca, the Liverpool hierarchy are ‘seriously considering’ taking up the option to sign Araujo permanently and would even be willing to do so immediately, but that clause can’t be activated until the end of this season.

The report adds that ‘everything indicates’ that the defender would be prepared to join the Reds outright if the Merseyside club were to push for a permanent transfer.

Barcelona aren’t considering a return to Camp Nou for the Uruguayan, with an acceptance that they’re powerless to bring him back if LFC were to pay the purchase clause, and it’s deemed ‘highly unlikely’ that he’d revert to his parent club from next summer.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

With the Catalan club not necessarily resigned to their fate, but realising that they don’t hold the balance of power over Araujo, it feels increasingly as though he could become a Liverpool player outright in 2027.

Considering the all-action performances that the Uruguay international has been putting in at Anfield, and that we could lose the experience of Virgil van Dijk and Joe Gomez from our defence if neither sign new contracts, the Reds would be foolish not to try and activate the purchase option.

The 27-year-old seems quite happy to remain on Merseyside for the long-term, by all accounts, and Liverpool would buy him in the knowledge that he’s already proven he can thrive in the Premier League.

If he maintains the performance levels he’s shown so far at LFC throughout a full season, then £47m would seem a very fair outlay for Araujo, who’s helped to stabilise what had been a highly volatile right-back position in our line-up.

It’s frustrating in one sense that we have to wait until the end of the campaign to activate the purchase option, but unless there’s a major plot twist between now and May, we’re confident that a permanent transfer will ultimately be completed and he’ll be a Liverpool player outright in a few months’ time.

Correspondent AUTHORITY NCTJ-qualified football journalist with experience at VAVEL, Hayters TV, SPORTbible, and Centredevils. He provides specialist tactical and analytical content to ensure fans get beyond the headlines and understand the full picture.

Liverpool forward Cody Gakpo struggled to have any impact as the Netherlands were thrashed 5-0 by Germany in the Nations League on Monday.

Derry Scherhant, Florian Wirtz, Nico Schlotterbeck and Brajan Gruda got the goals for the home side, on what was a truly embarrassing night for Xavi Hernandez's team.

The Dutch arrived in Berlin with the top spot in group two almost wrapped up, needing just to avoid defeat by more than three goals after they had boosted their goal difference by seven against Greece on Friday.

Gakpo, 27, failed to score in that game and he had even less of an impact against Germany, faltering in the face of his former manager Jurgen Klopp.

The winger has not looked quite the same since returning from injury, with his fitness still looking to be in question.

He has scored just once since making his return, with that strike coming from the penalty spot against Chelsea in the Carabao Cup.

Though Gakpo has been starting on the right of the attack for Liverpool of late, he will soon find his position under threat.

Both Victor Munoz and Rio Ngumoha have been in good form in the position, and will hope to usurp their senior.

Right now, the 27-year-old is doing little to argue against exactly that, producing another disappointing display on Monday.

In Gakpo's defence, he was not alone in struggling against the onslaught of German attacks, but he is considered a leader and held to higher expectations.

The forward misplaced a whopping 12 passes in his 78 minutes on the pitch, was dispossessed once and dribbled past twice.

He took only two touches in the opposition box and lost five duels, in what was a dismal display.

Dutch outlet Voetbal Primeur gave Gakpo a 4.5 out of 10, and added: "The attacker showed a few nice flashes, especially shortly after half-time, and injected some life into the game, but even Gakpo couldn't turn the tide. He just stood there and watched."

In an equally harsh verdict, Soccernews gave him a four and said: "Not a great international spell for the Liverpool left winger. Against Greece, he was the only attacker without any impact, and in Berlin, he was invisible except for one attempt.

"When it came to tracking back with the score at 3-0, he refused to make an extra effort. Xavi won't like that."

Upon their return to action, Liverpool will face a difficult run of fixtures and Andoni Iraola will look for leaders.

The Reds will host Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United at Anfield on Sunday before facing Everton in the Merseyside derby and Chelsea soon after.

Gakpo will be one face that Iraola will certainly expect contribution from, and he must ensure that he provides it.

If not, his position on the right will almost certainly be under siege from the younger forwards behind him.

Chile return to action for their final game of the year on Tuesday aiming to bow out on a positive note after a tough year.

La Roja faced no competitive action in 2026, having fallen short in South American World Cup qualifying last year, meaning they have played just eight times prior to Tuesday's upcoming fixture, losing five and winning three of those.

Nicolas Cordova's team did end the September and October international break with a 2-0 victory over Mexico, thanks to goals from Maximiliano Gutierrez and Vicente Pizarro, but they failed to carry that into the final break of the term, falling short against Colombia again away from home last Saturday.

A trip to Cali ended in a 1-0 loss for La Roja, their fifth defeat in seven games while failing to score for a second time and making it a sixth game against Colombia without a win since a 2019 Copa America penalty shootout triumph.

Now taking their turn to have home advantage for the reverse fixture in Santiago, Chile will set out to end the year with a victory before looking forward and aiming to build in the new year.

Their visitors, meanwhile, make the trip to Santiago aiming to round off their positive year with a double over Chile.

Colombia's 2026 will be remembered for a creditable showing at the World Cup in USA, Mexico and Canada, as La Tricolor topped their group on seven points with two wins and a draw against Portugal.

They would then get past Ghana thanks to Jhon Arias's goal, before falling just short at the hands of Switzerland in the round of 16, losing a penalty shootout after a goalless draw.

In four friendlies since, Nestor Lorenzo's team have won twice, firstly ending the September and October break by beating Peru 2-0 before they beat Chile in Cali on Saturday with a first-half own goal from Guillermo Maripan making the difference.

Now on seven wins in 13 games in the calendar year, Colombia head to Chile looking to make it a perfect final break of 2026 and record another victory.

Nicolas Cordova has a relatively inexperienced Chile squad for the November friendlies, with defenders Paulo Diaz and Benjamin Kuscevic and Paulo Diaz missing out while key midfielder Marcelino Nunez is also not involved.

Ben Brereton Diaz boasts the most experience in a young attacking unit, with 46 caps and 10 international goals to his name, and he may come in from the outset after a substitute appearance in the last game.

That is after Gutierrez, Gonzalo Tapia and Crystal Palace prospect Dario Osorio started in a front three in Colombia, while Rodrigo Echeverria, one of just four players aged above 30 years old, should continue in midfield alongside Vicente Pizarro.

Colombia have also seen plenty of change in their squad, particularly since the World Cup, with James Rodriguez, Juan Quintero and David Ospina retiring while Juan Cuadrado, Santiago Arias, Yerry Mina, Richard Rios and Jhon Duran are also not involved.

Arguably the most notable omission is injured Bayern Munich winger Luis Diaz, leaving La Tricolor light and inexperienced up top.

The line should again be led by Luis Suarez, who has eight goals in 21 caps and 13 in 15 appearances across the Primeira Liga and Champions League for Sporting Lisbon, while a new look squad is headlined by the likes of Daniel Munoz, Davinson Sanchez and Jefferson Lerma.

Vigouroux; Villagra, Maripan, Ulloa; Loyola, Echeverria, Pizarro, Suazo; Osorio, Brereton Diaz, Gutierrez

#1923. Man City: Why the international break could be vital for Maresca

By Axel Clody | 16 Nov 2026 06:59

Manchester City began the season with the impression that adapting to Enzo Maresca’s work would be quick. With seven wins in the opening Premier League rounds, the team took the lead and at one point opened up a six-point advantage over Arsenal. The run, however, was abruptly interrupted.

Defeats to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest dropped the team to third place and allowed the current champions to pull clear at the top.

More than the scorelines, the performances exposed difficulties in competing physically, winning duels and protecting the defence when possession is lost. Maresca himself acknowledged that his team could not keep up with the intensity of the opposition in the first half.

So the November international break comes at a good time. The pause will not erase the problems that have appeared in recent weeks, nor does it mean that all the players will have days off. But it offers the manager a valuable opportunity to assess performance, recover players and work on adjustments that would hardly be possible with a run of matches.

The drop in City’s level cannot be explained only by a lack of efficiency in front of goal.

The team can still control possession and produce offensive volume. Against Forest, for example, it finished the game with 79 per cent possession and 12 shots. The problem is that this control has not been enough to stop opponents finding space and creating dangerous situations.

One of the main issues is defensive protection. City have conceded 17 goals in eight matches and have not kept a clean sheet in any of their last nine games. The high defensive line, a hallmark of Maresca’s teams, demands coordination between the units and a quick ability to react to losing the ball. When the counter-press does not work, the defenders are left exposed to fast attacks and have to defend large spaces.

The absence of Rodri helps to explain part of this difficulty. The Spaniard offered reading of the game, interceptions and the quality to organise the build-up. More than a defensive midfielder who protects the defence, he is a player capable of anticipating danger and stopping counter-attacks before they gather speed. Without him, the rest of the midfield has to share responsibilities that Rodri used to take on almost alone.

Elliot Anderson has been important in this context, but so too is the distribution of roles. The presence of players such as Enzo Fernandez and Rayan Cherki adds technical quality and creativity, but also demands defensive cover. If the two play together without a structure that protects the central area, Anderson can be overburdened in covering and in physical duels.

The break allows Maresca to work on these relationships. One possibility is to adjust the make-up of the midfield, ensuring more balance between creation and protection. Another is to review the team’s positioning without the ball, especially the distance between the defensive line and the most advanced players. It is not necessarily a question of abandoning the style of play, but of finding ways to make it less vulnerable.

The calendar and the physical condition of the squad are another important aspect. City lost rhythm during a demanding period of fixtures, and the recovery of players can help the team regain the intensity needed to execute Maresca’s model.

It will also be important to monitor the situation of Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol. Both were substituted at half-time against Nottingham Forest because of physical problems, according to Maresca. The break could be useful to assess the extent of the issues and avoid important players returning before they are fully fit.

There is, however, a caveat: the international break is not a holiday for the whole squad. Several starters have been called up by their national teams, among them Erling Haaland, Gianluigi Donnarumma, Ruben Dias, Gvardiol, Guehi, Enzo Fernandez and Cherki. Travel and international commitments reduce the recovery time for some players, while others will be able to stay in Manchester and work directly with the coaching staff.

Even so, the break offers an opportunity to reorganise the workload and prepare the squad for what follows. In a season in which intensity is essential to the functioning of Maresca’s system, managing physical wear and tear is also part of the recovery process.

The break arrives at a time when City need to recover not only results, but also confidence in their own way of playing. The seven opening wins showed that the team has the resources to compete for the title. The three defeats that followed, on the other hand, revealed that there are still important adjustments to be made to sustain that level over an entire season.

The first challenge after the break will be against Fulham at the Etihad Stadium. Then the team will face an even more significant fixture: the visit to Arsenal on 29 November. The six-point gap makes the direct meeting an important opportunity to close the distance, although the result will not be enough, by itself, to settle the title race.

For Maresca, the international break is a chance to find answers before the run of negative results turns into an even bigger problem. The manager needs to restore defensive solidity, find the best distribution of roles in midfield and make possession dominance translate into effective control of matches again.

City do not need to abandon their identity to react. Above all, they need to find a better balance between what they do with the ball and what they can do when they lose it. If the break allows Maresca to progress with this work and recover important players, the team could return better prepared to face a decisive stretch of the season.

#1920. ‘Go and do it’ – Jamie Carragher issues January transfer plea to Liverpool chiefs

Jamie Carragher has urged Liverpool to be active in the January transfer window if ‘a certain type’ of player becomes attainable.

The Reds have made some major mid-season signings in the past, with Virgil van Dijk, Daniel Sturridge, Luis Suarez, Philippe Coutinho and Luis Diaz all joining in the winter months, but they haven’t entered the January market for an immediate new addition since landing Cody Gakpo nearly four years ago.

The window will open in just over six weeks’ time, so speculation over prospective new arrivals will no doubt intensify in the lead-up to New Year’s, and Carragher feels that his former club must be proactive if they spot the right market opportunity.

Speaking on The Overlap Fan Debate, the ex-Liverpool defender said: “For me, this season for [Andoni] Iraola is about making sure we’re in a position for next season to really challenge for the title, so I think every transfer window is rightly important.

“The areas on the pitch for Liverpool that still stand out for me – and we’ve got Hugo Ekitike to come back as well, so that’ll fix the back-up for Alexander Isak, or maybe play alongside Isak – is the full-back area.

“If there’s a left-back, they’ve got to go and do it in January. Or a midfield player, a certain type of midfield player. It’s not about what we did with [Jurgen] Klopp, where we’d wait for the summer, because this feels like it’s the here and now.”

One thing the Reds have proven quite adept at in previous Januarys is making a late surge to snare a mid-season signing, like they did when stealing in for Diaz in 2022 and Gakpo the following winter.

It’s notable that the Dutchman was signed when Julian Ward was Liverpool’s sporting director, and he’s now back in that job title for a second spell, having shown in the past that he’s prepared to pounce for the right opportunity.

Carragher’s reservations about the full-back berths are understandable. Both Jeremie Frimpong and Conor Bradley on the right have been hampered by injury issues, while Kostas Tsimikas hasn’t been able to provide stern competition for Milos Kerkez on the other flank.

LFC won’t enter the January market for the sake of it and won’t be swayed by external opinion, no matter how voluble it might be, but that isn’t to say that they definitely won’t bring in a new signing or two during the winter window.

Liverpool’s transfer strategy could also be swayed by what happens over the coming weeks, and whether they go into the New Year with Andoni Iraola worryingly light in some positions.

Carragher is spot-on about one thing – if there’s a smart deal to be done in January, then Ward must swoop in straight away rather than biding his time for next summer.

#1907. How Scotland can qualify for Nations League playoffs, and how third place finish affects Euro 2028 qualifiers

Scotland end their Nations League campaign with a clash against Switzerland on Monday, with their slim hopes of qualifying for the promotion playoffs still intact.

Placed in Group B1 alongside Slovenia, North Macedonia and the aforementioned Switzerland, new head coach Sebastien Pocognoli kept alive Scotland’s chances of claiming second spot in the group with a narrow 2-1 home win over North Macedonia on Friday, thanks to two goals from John McGinn.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Here’s what Scotland needs to happen to nab a promotion/relegation playoff spot, how to watch the draw and what a third-placed finish would mean for Pocognoli’s men.

First and foremost, Scotland MUST beat Switzerland to stand any chance of finishing in second place in the group. Should they achieve that, they will also have to hope Slovenia fail to beat North Macedonia. If Slovenia beat North Macedonia this evening, it is impossible for Scotland to finish in second place regardless of their result against Switzerland.

In the scenario that Scotland draw with Switzerland, and Slovenia lose to North Macedonia, both sides would be level on eight points. However, Slovenia would take second place following their 2-1 win at Hampden Park last month, with UEFA prioritizing head-to-head results between tied teams rather than overall goal difference. Currently in third place on seven points, they trail Slovenia in second place on eight points.

The draw for the Nations League playoffs will take place on Friday, 20 November. The draw begins at 11am UK time and will take place at UEFA headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland.

You can stream the draw live via your smart TV, laptop, tablet or mobile phone, the entire ceremony will be streamed for free via UEFA.tv and the official UEFA YouTube channel.

If Scotland fail to beat Switzerland in their final Group B1 game, they will be guaranteed to finish in the third place and will remain in League B for the next edition of the tournament. North Macedonia are already guaranteed to finish fourth place will face a promotion/relegation playoff game with a second-placed League C team to remain in League B. Scotland are safe from relegation to League B.

Meanwhile, Switzerland have already won the group and have been promoted to League A. As detailed above, the second place team [currently Slovenia] will face a playoff against a third placed League A side.

A third placed finish will have a direct effect on Scotland’s Euro 2028 qualifying campaign, which begins in March 2027. The tournament, which takes place across the United Kingdom and the Republic of Ireland, will require all four co-hosts - England, Scotland, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland - to compete in the standard qualifying campaign. They are not given a bye.

Where teams finish in their Nations League groups will directly decide how they are seeded for Euro 2028 qualifying, with each nation seeded based on their final group position. If Scotland finish in third, then Pocognoli’s side would drop into pot three for the draw, which could result in them facing high-ranking opponents from Pot 1 and Pot 2.

The Euro 2028 qualifying draw sees teams separated into 12 groups of either four or five teams. Those who win their groups groups qualify automatically for the finals, alongside the eight highest ranked second place finishers. The four lowest ranked second place finishers enter the play-offs. Team who finish third or lower will not qualify.

The one caveat is that the host nations have two spots in the finals reserved if they fail to qualify. If more than two host teams do not qualify via the usual route, these two places will be allocated to the hosts placed highest in the European Qualifiers overall rankings. If only one or neither of the spots be used, the remaining places will be reallocated via the play-offs.

#1903. Hearts sporting director addresses January transfer plans, ‘unprecedented’ injuries and recent form

Sporting director Graeme Jones has pinpointed European football and a new playing style among the key reasons for Hearts' "unprecedented" injury situation.

The Tynecastle side were missing 11 first-team players for most recent match - a 5-2 home defeat by Falkirk before the international break - and then lost another when Malachi Fagan-Walcott limped off.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The absences have coincided with a run of just one win in eight matches across all competitions, leaving Wouter Vrancken's side fourth in the Scottish Premiership and 32nd in the Uefa Conference League.

"I need to look beyond the bad luck theory and dig into possible circumstances or reasons as to why we find ourselves where we are," Jones said in a club interview. "We've got a new head coach that's brought in an intended new front foot style philosophy of how we play. We have new players who are adapting to a more competitive league than what they've been used to previously.

"We have European football which is becoming the standard we want every season but the demands that Thursday-Sunday brings on the team. And then there's also the part of the bad luck which is we've suffered a huge amount of contact injuries so far this season, more in this short period than the whole of last season.

"So, unfortunate as it is, it's a convergence of all these factors. But I also think it's important to realise that there is light at the end of the tunnel. We have players returning for the game coming up on Saturday [away to Dundee].

"We're hoping to have up to six, maybe even seven players possibly back into contention for first team training. Whether they're included in the squad, it just might be too soon, but we'll manage that accordingly. I can be confident that things are going to improve in the second half of the season, I've got no doubts on that."

Jones reassured fans that Hearts are "not sitting on our hands" with regards to addressing their injury issues.

He added: "We conducted an external review of our performance area at the turn of this year. We utilised one of the top performance practitioners in the the UK and he conducted an in-depth review that came with a numerous recommendations of things that we needed to improve. We've implemented all of these things.

"We have invested heavily in our medical department and even though it might not feel like it from the outside looking in, we're in a much better place to deal with this unprecedented level of injuries than we would have been a year ago."

Hearts came into the campaign looking to build on last season's runners-up finish in the Scottish Premiership after narrowly missing out on a first title in 66 years to Celtic on the final day. However, after 12 matches, they have collected 10 points less than they had at the same stage last season with 12 more goals conceded. They also lost their 18-month unbeaten home record against Falkirk and were beaten by rivals Hibs at Hampden for the first time in the semi-finals of the Premier Sports Cup.

"It's not been good enough," Jones admitted. "I know that, Wouter knows that, the players know that and we're doing everything during this international week to recalibrate and rest and put things right as best we can.

"It's important to have the big picture in mind when you're in my role and looking towards the future. But I totally understand the short-term results have a massive effect on the general harmony across the board, particularly with our fans.

"I would never sit here and tell fans to be patient and calm during these periods. I am a fan, I've sat in the stand during some of the worst times throughout the club's history so I do understand. But we as a club and me as the sporting director have to remain focused on the objectives and the long-term future of the club and the success of the club that we are striving for."

Addressing Hearts' plans for the January transfer window, Jones, who was appointed sporting director two years ago, said the focus would be on balancing the squad.

"We've got a very large squad with double figures number of players that are unavailable recently so as they return back we will naturally have to look at creating balance within the squad," he said. "So we will look to decrease the size of the squad but also only add with quality. So it will be an active window like all transfer windows are but as we all know January is notoriously difficult.

"We've got plenty of evidence in the last two years that the players that sign in January don't always come in and hit the ground running. So we have to focus our attentions on the quality that can make a difference but we will be very much looking to create a bit of balance within the squad. Once all our players come back are fit and available and then looking to add quality and also help people move on that aren't getting the opportunities."

“That’s why I call it a “gamble”: I wanted him at Milan at all costs, even though he hadn’t played for a year and had essentially disappeared from the radar. I was heavily criticized. But, I repeat, I was convinced I had a boy with enormous potential on my hands.

“Initially, we played him on the left flank, with an inverted foot, to allow him to cut inside and shoot. But it was clear to me that he had all the makings of a great playmaker. When I suggested it to the right people, they called me crazy…

“Leaving for zero? Don’t make me think about it… It’s unspeakable, unbelievable.”

But while the hosts can relax, the game is not a dead rubber for Scotland, who can still claim a runners-up finish in the section with what would be a famous away victory over the side ranked 12th in the Fifa world rankings - 31 places above them.

The game is also hugely significant for captain Andy Robertson who will become Scotland’s most capped player, eclipsing Kenny Dalglish by reaching 103 appearances, if he plays on the night as expected.

It would also guarantee pot two seeding for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw, which takes place next month. If Scotland finish third in Nations League B1, they will drop into pot three and face high-ranking teams in pots one and two.

The Nations League B1 fixture between Switzerland and Scotland takes place at Berit Sitterstadion in St. Gallen on Monday, November 16, 2026. Kick-off is 7.45pm.

The match will be broadcast live on BBC 2 and the BBC Scotland channel with coverage starting at 7.30pm.

The game can be live streamed for free on the BBC Sport website and the BBC iPlayer.

Scotland picked up no fresh injury concerns against North Macedonia on Friday but head coach Sebastien Pocognoli is expected to make changes. “I will need to consider the best approach for the game regarding the quality and also the fitness of some players,” he said. “We have some players in the squad who we have to manage. They cannot play two games in a row.”

Switzerland, meanwhile, are expected to rotate their squad. Head coach Murat Yakin will be without Internazionale defender Manuel Akanji, captain Granit Xhaka of Sunderland, Aston Villa's Johan Manzambi and Nottingham Forest winger Dan Ndoye. Yakin revealed that 20-year-old Sion striker Winsley Boteli will earn his fourth senior cap, while 23-year-old Young Boys midfielder Alvyn Sanches will be handed his seventh, both from the start.

The entire officiating team is from the Netherlands with referee Danny Makkelie taking charge on the field. He is joined by assistant referees Hessel Steegstra and Jan de Vries, with Alex Bos acting as the fourth official. Erwin Blank serves as the Video Assistant Referee (VAR), who will be joined in the VAR booth by Jeroen Manschot.

Switzerland 17/20, Draw 29/10, Scotland 7/2 - via oddschecker.com.

#1896. When did Scotland last beat Switzerland? Full head to head record and last five games

Scotland’s Nations League campaign wraps up on Monday evening with a tough encounter against Switzerland as the side aims to snatch an unlikely promotion playoff spot in Group B1 from Slovenia.

Head coach Sebastien Pocognoli finally got his first home win with a 2-1 win over North Macedonia on Friday, and now his team will look to make it back-to-back wins for the first time under his management while hoping Slovenia slip up in the group’s other game.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

However, should Scotland fail to win in St Gallen, hopes of promotion back to League A will be extinguished. A third-place finish will also have ramifications for the upcoming Euro 2028 qualifiers, which are drawn in Belfast this December.

But when did Scotland last beat Switzerland? What is their head-to-head record, and when did they last meet? Here’s everything you need to know about Scotland’s record against Switzerland.

The teams have faced each other a total of 18 times, and have met twice in major tournament finals, with both encounters taking place in the group stage of the European Championships.

They last faced each other just last month in the Nations League, where Switzerland ran out 3-0 winners after Jack Hendry was sent off early on at Hampden Park. Prior to that game, they drew 1-1 at Euro 2024 in Germany, with Scott McTominay opening the scoring early on for Scotland, before Xherdan Shaqiri equalised shortly afterwards.

From their 18 games played, Scotland have eight wins, giving them a 33.3% win percentage. Switzerland have won a total of six times - a 22.22 per cent win percentage. A further four games have ended in a draw.

Despite having the better head to head record against the Swiss, the Scotland men’s national team have not tasted victory against them for over 30 years. Their most recent win came at Euro 1996 at Villa Park, Birmingham on 18 June, where they earned their first win a 1-0 win in their final group game at the tournament.

The victory came via a fine strike from Ally McCoist in the 36th minute, but was not enough for Scotland to qualify for the knockout stages of the tournament, with the Netherlands finishing above them on goal difference. The Switzerland side that day included future Celtic defender Ramon Vega.

Scotland line up that night: Andy Goram, Tom Boyd, Colin Calderwood, Colin Hendry, Stuart McCall, Gary McAllister, John Collins, Tosh McKinlay (Scott Booth, 60), Craig Burley, Gordon Durie and Ally McCoist (John Spencer, 84).

29 September 2026: Scotland 0-3 Switzerland (Nations League)

19 June 2024: Scotland 1-1 Switzerland (Euro 2024)

1 March 2006: Scotland 1-3 Switzerland (Friendly)

18 June 1996: Scotland 1-0 Switzerland (Euro 1996)

8 September 1993: Scotland 1-1 Switzerland (World Cup 1994 Qualifier)
